long_description:
**Atlanta Tech Week is in town, so let's do lunch.**
Bytes & Bites is our casual, community-driven lunch where technologists of all backgrounds come together to connect, swap ideas, and build relationships over good food. This one's a special edition during Atlanta Tech Week, so whether you're an Atlanta regular or in town for ATW, pull up a chair.
No talks, no slides, no forced networking. Just tech folks, good food, and real conversation. Deep in code, leading teams, or just starting out? This is your space to take a break, meet people, and talk shop (or not).
🗓️ **When:** Friday, August 14 · 11:45 AM–1:30 PM
Swing by when you can, no need to stay the whole time.
📍 **Where:** Krog Street Market · 99 Krog Street NE, Atlanta, GA
🍽️ **What to expect:**

* Tons of [food options](https://www.thekrogdistrict.com/directory) inside the market
* Easy, low-pressure conversation
* No agenda, just lunch and good company
* A friendly crowd from across Atlanta's tech communities (and a few ATW visitors)

**Finding us:** Look for the tables with the REFACTR.TECH signs and come say hi.
**Parking & getting there:**

* On-site parking garage and surface lot available
* All visitors register and pay for parking on arrival (QR code, text-to-pay, or pay stations)
* Garage rates start around $4 for the first hour before 4 pm; surface lot has a 3-hour max during the day
* More parking and transit details: [https://www.thekrogdistrict.com/visit](https://www.thekrogdistrict.com/visit)

Come as you are, bring a friend, grab something tasty, and let's build community over lunch.
Questions or trouble finding us? Drop a comment here or ask in the **#ask-us** channel in our [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/qyUw9D6sqR).

*Everyone participating in REFACTR.TECH events and our Discord/Slack community, including attendees, speakers, sponsors, and volunteers, agrees to our [code of conduct](https://refactr.tech/code-of-conduct). Organizers will enforce this code throughout the event.*

long_description:
🌑 New Moon in Leo: Yoga & Sound Bath
Friday, August 14th • 7:30 PM

Step into the radiant energy of the New Moon in Leo for an evening of movement, mindfulness, and deep vibrational healing.

The New Moon marks the beginning of a new lunar cycle a powerful time to plant seeds of intention, embrace fresh starts, and reconnect with your authentic self. In the bold, heart-centered sign of Leo, this lunation encourages you to shine unapologetically, express your creativity, strengthen your confidence, and lead your life with courage and joy. Leo reminds us that our greatest magic comes from living authentically and allowing our inner light to be seen.

We'll begin the evening with gentle, beginner friendly yoga to awaken the body and open the heart, followed by calming breathwork designed to quiet the mind and center your energy. From there, you'll be guided through a meditation focused on setting intentions, connecting with your inner strength, and welcoming the opportunities this New Moon has to offer.

We'll then settle into a deeply restorative sound bath, where the healing vibrations of quartz crystal singing bowls, a gong, chimes, and other magical sound healing instruments will wash over you. Allow the frequencies to help release stagnant energy, restore balance, and create space for the intentions you've planted under this powerful New Moon

Whether you're looking to relax, recharge, deepen your spiritual practice, or simply enjoy a peaceful evening surrounded by like-minded souls, this experience offers the perfect opportunity to reset your mind, body, and spirit.

✨ No experience is necessary. Please wear comfortable clothing and bring a yoga mat, blanket, pillow, or anything else that will help you fully relax during the sound bath.

Space is limited, so reserve your spot early and join us as we welcome a new cycle filled with confidence, creativity, and heart-centered intention. 🌑🦁✨

long_description:
If you have any specific health limitations, please make teacher aware before start of class.

◼️Bring your own yoga mat.
◼️Bring water bottle to stay hydrated.
◼️Bring what you need for ultimate comfort. 👜 During sound bath, you'll want to have put your socks back on and on with a sweater or hoodie. Even if it's a hot day, the AC will be on indoors. When the body goes into a state of relaxation, the body temperature drops. Help yourself be as cozy as possible by bringing what is needed for that. Recommended items for the guided relaxation:
▪️ an eye-mask or small towel to cover eyes
▪️ blanket to stay warm/cozy when temperature drops as body shifts into state of relaxation
▪️ decorative size pillow for under the head

A shared yoga practice isn't the time for creating social media content. No recording audio or visual.
Please respect the privacy of everyone in attendance and have phone off before the start of class.

**For security, the exterior doors remain locked from the outside at all times. Your instructor will be at the entrance to greet and let you in between 9:45 a.m. and 9:55 a.m.**
**​Please arrive 15 minutes early. Once class begins at 10:00 a.m., the instructor will be in the sanctuary and unable to open the door, so late arrivals cannot be accommodated.**
​*Note: The doors feature exit push bars, so you can safely leave the building at any time.*

title: Tantra Retreat
venue_name: DoubleTree Resort by Hilton Hotel Paradise Valley - Scottsdale
description: Tantra Retreat
long_description:
Three days that change how connection feels in your body, your relationship, and your everyday life.

If intimacy feels like it belonged to a version of you who had more time, more ease, more fire…

And now it feels rushed. Scheduled. Negotiated.

You’re not broken.

You’re disconnected.

It's time to stop wondering where that part of you went.

Tantra is the gateway back to that version of you.

The version of you who felt:

more open

more confident

more present in your body

less guarded around touch, desire, and connection.

Tantra, in it's original form, was never about performance or technique alone.

It was an initiation into conscious love.

A discipline of awareness.

A sacred path that teaches how breath, attention, presence, and sexual energy shape connection itself.

This immersive retreat introduces both foundational and more advanced Tantric principles translated into a modern, trauma-informed framework grounded in neuroscience, somatic awareness, and relational psychology.

You will not simply learn techniques.

You will experience the deeper architecture of intimacy. You'll unlock how energy moves between bodies, how presence shapes arousal, how awareness transforms connection.

You’re not alone.

And you’re not broken.

For many people, intimacy doesn’t disappear.

It slowly becomes harder to access.

You start noticing things like:

Overthinking instead of feeling

Tension where there used to be ease

Desire that feels inconsistent or distant

Touch that feels expected instead of inviting

Connection that requires effort instead of happening naturally

This isn’t about chemistry.

It’s about nervous system safety.

And most of us were never taught how intimacy works in the body.

This Retreat Is About Changing How Intimacy Feels From The Inside Out

Whether you are single or partnered, intimacy begins with your ability to:

stay present instead of shutting down

receive without bracing

communicate desire without fear

experience pleasure without

long_description:
**This event is posted on behalf of the Westerly Land Trust. Registration is required outside of Meetup. [Please register here.](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/paddle-yoga-float-flow-registration-1993347180075)**

Certified yoga teacher, Janice Fifer, will guide us through Sun Salutations with a focus on hip and shoulder openers to prepare for a paddle up the Pawcatuck River. We will stop along the way for a short meditation and ride the river’s gentle current back to the put-in point. The day will end with relaxation and a closing circle. This is a moderate paddle for kayakers with some experience, with the emphasis on relaxing and enjoying nature.

**What to bring:** BYO Kayak, Paddle board, canoe etc, Paddle, Life Jacket, Yoga Mat, Large Towel (to put under your yoga mat), Water, Bug Repellent. Be aware that your shoes will get wet and muddy.

**Please note:** Rhode Island State Regulations require that everyone, regardless of age, MUST wear a US Coast Guard approved life jacket, fastened in the manner the manufacturer intended.

**Parking:** Parking is available at Flora Whitely Preserve at [197 Potter Hill Rd](https://www.google.com/maps/place/197+Potter+Hill+Rd,+Westerly,+RI+02891/@41.4137429,-71.7974699,21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x89e5dd6e2199da8f:0xd825c68fe1fa552!8m2!3d41.4136666!4d-71.797423?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYyOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D "https://www.google.com/maps/place/197+Potter+Hill+Rd,+Westerly,+RI+02891/@41.4137429,-71.7974699,21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x89e5dd6e2199da8f:0xd825c68fe1fa552!8m2!3d41.4136666!4d-71.797423?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYyOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D"). **Hope you’re having a great weekend! Addy (Rishabh) here, checking in about this week’s gathering.**

**🎵 Live Music — Inviting temple friends who play vocals, harmonium, mridanga, kartals, or any instrument. Bring your instrument if you’d like to join in - otherwise just bring your voice and heart. Bring water too!**

**This is a call-and-response kirtan practice — known to support emotional balance through stress, isolation, and the heavier stuff life throws at us. No experience needed. Just follow along and sing.**

**United States**

long_description:
Please join us for a weekend of coastal retreat in Yachats, Oregon this summer, 2026 - for a memorable experience, including Farm to Table meal tasting and restorative yoga!

**Info and Registration:**
[https://solfoodnutrition.com/retreatswithiris](https://solfoodnutrition.com/retreatswithiris)

What Awaits You:
**Yoga & Nervous System Healing** — Anne will be leading five sessions of gentle hatha and yin yoga along with breathwork, meditation, acupressure and self massage. Each practice will weave together nervous system restoration, insightful self-inquiry, and spiritual wisdom.
**Farm-to-Table Cooking Immersion** — A hands-on community cooking experience led by Registered Dietitian and cookbook author, Iris Briand. This isn't a cooking class so much as a reclamation of the kitchen as a place of pleasure and healing. Seasonal whole foods, practical nourishment tips, recipes to take home — and then sitting down together to taste what you made.
**Forest Bathing Experience** — An intentional guided walk through the stunning coastal forest, using nature itself as medicine to calm the nervous system, quiet the mind, and return you to presence.
**The Magical Oregon Coast in Late Summer** — Golden light. Ocean air. The sea at its warmest and most generous.

Retreat Hosts:
**Iris Briand** — a registered dietician, organic farmer, and cookbook author whose work beautifully embodies the healing wisdom of seasonal nourishment and whole foods.
**Anne Witmer** — Yoga teacher extraordinaire, with over 20 years of yoga teaching experience and leading retreats.

**Info and Registration:**
[https://solfoodnutrition.com/retreatswithiris](https://solfoodnutrition.com/retreatswithiris)

Looking forward to seeing you there.
-Iris and Anne

long_description:
Drop the kids off for intentional, guided practice on the pottery wheel, or stay & play too! Ages 8+

Ongoing: Fridays, 6:00pm - 8:00pm. $40.
Ages 8-Adult (Parents welcome!)

**Attendees must pre-register here:** https://www.catalystartscollaborative.com/service-page/family-clay-night-ages-8-fri-6pm-1

This ongoing class is designed for entry-level and experienced students alike, looking for more practice time on the pottery wheel. An experienced clay instructor will offer guided, small-group instruction for anyone interested in learning the basics of throwing on the pottery wheel. More advanced students are welcome to use this time to practice what they already know and try new tricks! After creating about 1-3 pieces, we will dry and fire their pieces for them. Most pieces are ready for pickup in 2-3 weeks.

Ceramics teach a number of valuable skills, including perseverance, patience, problem solving, and creativity! Bring your kiddos in to come play on the clay wheel and learn how to use this fun tool to create functional and decorative pieces, or join in on the fun and make some ceramic pieces of your own! The whole family is welcome!

***Details:***
**Registration is $40. Learn more about the class, your instructor, prerequisites, required materials, and register ahead of time here:** https://www.catalystartscollaborative.com/service-page/family-clay-night-ages-8-fri-6pm-1

long_description:
To Attend:

1. RSVP; then
2. Register at
https://www.eventbrite.com/e/evening-at-the-embassy-of-uganda-tickets-1996637269822

Experience a unique African cultural evening on foreign soil as we travel halfway across the world without ever leaving the District. Join us for a special night of Ugandan food, drinks, music, cultural dancing, diplomats, film, and more! Dress semi-smart casual and enjoy this unique party with the Ambassador and his staff at this African treasure of the Washington, D.C. area. (Indoor and Outdoor Celebration)

Featuring:

A) **African Food with a Ugandan Flavor:** Nyama Choma (beef served with kachumbari), goat stew (an East African favorite served with basmati rice and chapati), samosas, Ndengu (mungu beans in chicken broth seasoned with safari spice and cilantro), fruit, and more (TBA).

B) **Bar:** Sample the best and most unique Ugandan beers as well as other African treasures.

C) **Special Ugandan Musical and Dance Presentation**: Enjoy a world-renowned presentation of an authentic Ugandan tribal dance. Dressed in full authentic Ugandan costume with unusual African instruments, the dancers will treat us to a very unique performance of Ugandan music and dance, along with a cultural explanation as to each element’s origin, style, and meaning.

D) **Diplomatic Greeting:** Hear from the diplomats and feel free to schmooze the diplomatic staff.

E) **Ugandan Art**: Throughout the Embassy, the Ambassador has arranged for the presentation of special African artifacts and paintings unseen to most Americans’ eyes.

Scheduled to take place on the 15th of August, 2026, this will be a musical event like no other. The night will be filled with enchanting live performances, toe-tapping music, and an unforgettable party atmosphere as we come together to celebrate Pakistan's Independence Day in style. organizer: Laguna Hills Sound Bath Meetup Group
long_description:
Sound Bath at Well Connected Chiropractic

Once a month on a designated Saturday, we gather in Mission Viejo for an hour of sustained sound and deep rest. You arrive, you find a spot on the floor, you lie down, and the room fills with tone. Singing bowls, gong, rain sticks, chimes, and bells move sound through the space in long overlapping waves that the body registers as much as the ear does, and the nervous system tends to follow the sound down into a slower rhythm on its own.

Most people come in carrying a week of noise and leave in a state they describe as unusually quiet. Some drift into sleep, some stay awake and alert with eyes closed, some find images and memories moving through, and all of that belongs here. There is nothing to perform and nothing to get right, and the entire practice consists of lying still and letting sound do what sound does.

This is open to everyone regardless of experience. If you have never done anything like this, you belong in the room exactly as much as someone who has been sitting with sound for years.

What to bring: a yoga mat, a blanket, a pillow, and anything else that lets your body settle for an hour. Wear something comfortable enough to lie in.

Cost: $40, payable in cash or Venmo when you arrive.

Location: Well Connected Chiropractic, 26302 La Paz Rd, Unit 214, Mission Viejo, CA 92691. Date and start time are listed above.

A note: please arrive ten minutes early so we can begin together and keep the space undisturbed once sound starts. Space is limited by the size of the room, so RSVP if you plan to attend.

long_description:
Join us for an uplifting evening of devotion and community at our Bhakti Kirtan, guided by the inspiring Subala Das! Immerse yourself in the soulful vibrations of mantra chanting, led by Subal and passionate kirtaniyas who bring the sacred sounds to life. Kirtan is a beautiful practice of call-and-response singing that opens the heart, uplifts the spirit, and connects us with the divine through the practice of bhakti.

Bhakti, a Sanskrit word meaning “devotion” or “love,” is the spiritual path of connecting with the divine through heartfelt surrender and loving service. It emphasizes cultivating a deep, personal relationship with the divine, often expressed through music, prayer, and acts of kindness. Bhakti transcends religious boundaries, welcoming everyone into its embrace of universal love.

This event is open to everyone, whether you’re new to kirtan or a seasoned practitioner. Come as you are and leave feeling nourished—body, mind, and soul. Bring your friends and family, and experience the joy of chanting and sharing a meal together in a warm and welcoming atmosphere!

long_description:
## Rest Deeply. Heal Completely. Wake Up Restored.

Experience the profound healing power of **Yoga Nidra** \- the ancient practice of conscious relaxation also known as yogic sleep\. In this guided session with Kara\, you will be led into a deeply restful state between waking and sleeping\, where the body heals\, the mind quiets\, and the spirit renews\.

### What You Will Experience

* **Deep Physical Rest** \- Yoga Nidra is said to provide the equivalent of several hours of sleep in a single session
* **Mental Clarity** \- Release mental chatter\, stress\, and tension as you drop into a state of effortless awareness
* **Emotional Healing** \- Access deeper layers of the subconscious to release stored emotions and patterns
* **Guided by Kara** \- A warm\, experienced guide who holds space for your healing journey with care and intention

Whether you struggle with sleep, stress, or simply need a reset, this Yoga Nidra session offers a sanctuary of deep rest and renewal.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is Yoga Nidra?**
A: Yoga Nidra, or yogic sleep, is a guided meditation practice that brings you into a deeply relaxed state between waking and sleeping. It is used for stress relief, sleep improvement, emotional healing, and spiritual development.
**Q: Do I need any experience with yoga or meditation?**
A: No experience is needed. Yoga Nidra is accessible to everyone. You simply lie down, close your eyes, and follow Kara's gentle guidance.
**Q: How long is the session?**
A: Please refer to the session details for the exact duration. Yoga Nidra sessions typically range from 20 to 60 minutes.
**Q: Is this a digital or in-person session?**
A: Please refer to the product details or contact us to confirm the session format.

long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

long_description:
This book club is still forming! If you're interested, get on the waitlist and I'll be in touch. Note that dates / times / location may change.

**A woman’s desperate flight from an Apache raid unfolds into a sweeping tale of the Mexico–US border wars.**

Orchestrated with a stunningly imagined cast of characters, both historical and purely fictional, *Now I Surrender* radically recasts the story of how the West was “won.” In the contested borderlands between Mexico and the United States, a woman flees into the desert after a devastating raid on her dead husband’s ranch. A lieutenant colonel in service to the fledgling Republic, sent in pursuit of cattle rustlers, discovers he’s on the trail of a more dramatic abduction. Decades later, with political ambitions on the line, the American and Mexican militaries try to maneuver Geronimo, the most legendary of Apache warriors, into surrender. In our own day, a family travels through the region in search of a truer version of the past.

Part epic, part alt-Western, *Now I Surrender* is Álvaro Enrigue’s most expansive and impassioned novel yet. It weaves past and present, myth and history into a searing elegy for a way of life that was an incarnation of true liberty—and an homage to the spark in us that still thrills to its memory.

title: The Great Exhale: A Journey from Movement to Stillness
description: The practice of coming to life is a celebration; the practice of letting go is a liberation. In this 60-minute practice, we honor the full spectrum of the human experience. We begin by fueling the fire within, moving through a vinyasa flow designed to build heat, find rhythm, and invite you into a s
long_description:
The practice of coming to life is a celebration; the practice of letting go is a liberation. In this 60-minute practice, we honor the full spectrum of the human experience. We begin by fueling the fire within, moving through a vinyasa flow designed to build heat, find rhythm, and invite you into a state of total presence. This is the INHALE—the vibrant, active effort of being fully alive.

As we reach the peak of our movement, we transition into the The Great EXHALE. We shift from the "doing" to the "being," laying it all down for an extended, soulful relaxation and meditation.

In this space, we practice the art of "dying" to the day, the ego, and the effort. By meeting this stillness with a sense of joy and curiosity, we discover that the end of the movement is not a loss, but an entry point into profound peace.

What to expect:

☮️ Vibrant Flow: A high-energy sequence with music to get you out of your head and into your body.

✌️ Deep Release: A long, guided Savasana (deep rest) to integrate the physical work.

🧘‍♂️ Joyful Stillness: A philosophical exploration of surrender as a path to great peace.

Guided by Lauren Barlag

title: Socrates Café Rockville Meetup
description:
Socrates Cafés are gatherings around the world where people from different backgrounds get together and exchange thoughtful ideas and experiences while embracing the Socratic Method; the idea that we learn more when we question, and question with others.
Although this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Those attending decide upon the questions of the night. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, moral issues, and the first principl
long_description:
Socrates Cafés are gatherings around the world where people from different backgrounds get together and exchange thoughtful ideas and experiences while embracing the Socratic Method; the idea that we learn more when we question, and question with others.
Although this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Those attending decide upon the questions of the night. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, moral issues, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.
When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

long_description:
**“Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.” — Arthur C. Clarke**

Long before the bow and arrow, people found a way to throw a spear farther, faster and with more force than the human arm could manage alone.
The atlatl is one of humanity’s earliest force multipliers. It is a simple throwing lever, often no more than a carved stick with a hook or spur at one end, but it transformed hunting across much of the ancient world.
The tool extends the throwing arm, increasing leverage and accelerating a long, flexible dart toward its target. It is simple in appearance, but it teaches a great deal about physics, balance, coordination, material selection and the relationship between technology and the human body.

We’ll talk about how the atlatl works, why the darts are longer and more flexible than ordinary spears, and how leverage, timing and stored energy combine to create speed and force.
We’ll also look at the materials available to early makers, including wood, bone, antler, stone, sinew and plant fiber. We’ll discuss how atlatls differed across cultures and environments, and why this deceptively simple technology remained effective for thousands of years.

The main hands-on focus will be learning the throwing motion and safely practicing with atlatls and lightweight target darts. Depending on materials and time, we may also shape simple throwing boards and examine how dart length, flexibility, balance and weight affect performance.

long_description:
Modelface Comedy Club brings the best comics to Asheville, NC. We are so excited to have Tom Thakkar at AyurPrana Listening Room in West Asheville!!
Tom Thakkar is a comedian, podcaster, and writer living in Los Angeles, CA. He started his career in Bloomington, Indiana, where he was born and raised, a half Indian man with a deadbeat Indian father who he never met. Tom moved up the midwest circuit, and was named a New Face by the Just For Laughs festival in Montreal, and quickly moved to New York, and eventually to Los Angeles. He's now been seen on The Tonight Show starring Jimmy Fallon, CONAN, Comedy Central Presents, This Week at the Comedy Cellar, and much much more. In New York, he became a regular at the world famous Comedy Cellar, and works at almost every club in the city. He can also be heard as a regular on everybody's favorite new podcast "Are You Garbage," as well as on "We Might Be Drunk," "The Honeydew," "Doug Loves Movies," "Never Not Funny," "All Fantasy Everything," and more. Tom also hosted the Comedy Central podcast, "Stand Up with Tom Thakkar," and popular comedy/music podcast "Stand By Your Band," with Tommy McNamara.
On top of stand up and podcasting, Tom acted in the award winning short film "Sofa So Good" and wrote and appeared on the SyFy comedy sketch show, "The Movie Show." Right now, Tom can be seen touring around the country performing stand up almost every week, check his calendar to see if he’s coming to your city!
Featuring Sarah Love (AVL) and Noah Savage (NYC)

long_description:
**Are you ready to practice public speaking, improve your communication and build leadership skills?**

If the answer is YES, then you're in the right spot. Be A Voice Toastmasters is a nonprofit educational organization that offers a proven education program that helps improve communication and build leadership skills.

No matter where you are in your journey—whether you’re an experienced professional, student, entrepreneur, or emerging leader—Toastmasters offers a powerful, supportive space to grow. Here, you will strengthen your communication skills, speak with confidence, and learn to influence with clarity and purpose.

Along the way, you’ll sharpen your leadership abilities, become a more effective negotiator, and build the trust needed to inspire those around you. So, what are you waiting for? Find your voice and use it to create impact. **Join us at our next club meeting, held every 3rd Saturday at 10:30 AM EST.** Take that first step—show up, engage, and become the speaker and leader you are meant to be. We look forward to seeing you soon!

**Meeting Agenda**
• 10:20 AM Room Opens
• 10:30 AM Networking / Team Building Exercise
• 10:45 AM Welcome
• 11:00 AM Speakers
• 11:30 AM Table Topics
• 11:40 AM Speaker Evaluations
• 12:00 PM Meeting Adjournment

Contact the club president at contact-9720@toastmastersclubs.org for meeting location information.

"Suffused with the history and landscapes of the American West—its otherworldly flora and fauna, its rugged loggers and bridge builders—this extraordinary novella poignantly captures the disappearance of a distinctly American way of life.

Train Dreams tells the story of Robert Grainer, a day laborer in the American West at the start of the twentieth century—an ordinary man in extraordinary times. Buffeted by the loss of his family, Grainer struggles to make sense of this strange new world. As his story unfolds, we witness both his shocking personal defeats and the radical changes that transform America in his lifetime."

We will meet for brunch at James Provisions in Hurst.

title: FOG INDIA DAY
description: Celebrate the spirit of India like never before at FOG India Day in Fremont—one of the largest and most vibrant Indian cultural festivals in North America. Organized by the Federation of Indo-Americans of Northern California along with the Festival of Globe (FOG), this iconic event brings together thousands of people from diverse backgrounds to honor India’s Independence Day with pride, unity, and cultural richness. Held annually in the heart of Silicon Valley, the festival transforms the city into a lively celebration filled with color, music, and joy. The highlight of the event is the grand India Day Parade, featuring beautifully decorated floats, cultural showcases, and participation from various community organizations, reflecting the diversity of Indian heritage. Paseo Padre Parkway becomes the epicenter of festivities, hosting a spectacular lineup of activities. Visitors can enjoy live music and dance performances representing classical, folk, and contemporary styles from across India. The mela (fair) offers a rich experience with over 100 booths showcasing traditional crafts, ethnic fashion, delicious Indian cuisine, and community services. From shopping and food to entertainment and networking, there’s something for everyone.

No prior CAD experience is necessary. Bring a la
long_description:
**Details**
This hands-on class will teach you everything you need to know to get started with Onshape, a free browser-based CAD professional program. You'll learn the fundamentals of 3D modeling, creating assemblies of multiple parts into a working model, and how to design for manufacturability. By the end of the session, you'll have the skills to design your own parts for 3D printing, laser cutting, or CNC machining right here at the makerspace.
No prior CAD experience is necessary. Bring a laptop (or borrow one of ours), and we’ll teach you the rest. We'll work through a simple guided project together, so you leave with a real file you can take into the shop and start creating immediately. This class is a great starting point for anyone curious about product design, mechanical engineering, or just wanting to bring their own ideas to life using our tools. Space is limited, so sign up early to reserve your spot!

**How to Find Us**
Find us at HIVE Filament (2904 S W Temple St)

title: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening
description: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening Classes will guide you through complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual wisdom. An ongoing in-depth course deliving into profound wisdom within Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Hindu/Indian/Vedic spiritual philosophy, and Upanishads. You can see prior recordings at: YesVedanta.com/bg2 Timeless Wisdom of Bhagavad Gita: A Complete Course in Non-Duality in 700 Verses Join us for an in-depth exploration of the Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Vedantic wisdom. Our weekly live Zoom classes will guide you through the complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual knowledge. The Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue between Krishna (the teacher) and Arjuna (the student), addresses life's deepest questions: What is the nature of the Self? What is the highest purpose of existence? How can one live with intelligence and clarity? If all existence is One, why do we perceive differences? What is the nature of the universe and its origin? How can we understand the cause of the universe? How does one transcend the sense of limitation? This comprehensive study covers: The nature of the Self (Atman) and Reality (Brahman) Self-knowledge that includes dozens of methods to reveal your nature The role of karma, dharma, and free will The nature of the mind and consciousness (or awareness) The art of wise living and decision-making Cultivating emotional maturity and inner peace Through this course, you will: Grasp the core teachings of the Bhagavad Gita and their relevance to modern life Apply practical techniques for refining your thinking and mastering your emotions Develop a deeper understanding of your identity and the world Cultivate inner peace, clarity, and purpose This knowledge offers a step-by-step method to liberate the seeker from the confines of the ego, from the limitations imposed by the material world, and from the cycle of rebirth. W

long_description:
**Please reserve your spot at www.piesfitnessyoga.com**. The session is offered both InStudio and OnLine. The Zoom link for the OnLine session will be emailed 15 minutes before class starts to those who are registered at www.piesfitnessyoga.com. **Sign up for sessions must be made at least 2 hours prior to class.**

This therapeutic yin yoga class is specifically designed to help you connect your mind with your body, find your edges, soften your muscles to take the stretch deeper and into your connective tissues and fascia, and become more comfortable with stillness. Whether you just feel inflexible, are recuperating from an injury or procedure, or live with a chronic condition this class will meet you where you are and offer just the right postures to cultivate a greater sense of openness in your mind, body, and spirit.

Each posture is held for 3-5 minutes with support from props like blocks, bolsters, blankets, and more. You'll also learn visualization, meditation, and breath practices that will help you find more comfort in your discomfort on and off the mat.

title: Saturday Morning Yoga + Park Cleanup!
description:
Homies! This yoga class on Saturdays at 10am will be followed by a park cleanup each week. After ten years of teaching at Leahi Park it is long overdue to give back to the community and the park. At the end of the 10-11am yoga class, Homies that are able to stay will join me in picking up trash at Leahi Park and neighboring Makalei Park.

I have buckets and gloves for Homies to use, but you are also encouraged to bring your own supplies as I am hoping for many enthusiastic participants each week
long_description:
Homies! This yoga class on Saturdays at 10am will be followed by a park cleanup each week. After ten years of teaching at Leahi Park it is long overdue to give back to the community and the park. At the end of the 10-11am yoga class, Homies that are able to stay will join me in picking up trash at Leahi Park and neighboring Makalei Park.

I have buckets and gloves for Homies to use, but you are also encouraged to bring your own supplies as I am hoping for many enthusiastic participants each week. Any amount of time you can stay to help is appreciated. Any amount of trash collected makes a big difference. This is a small way to take yoga off of our mats and apply it in the world.

*All classes are free.*

Class is always on--rain or shine!

description: In philosophy, the "state of nature" is the hypothetical way of life that existed before humans organized themselves into societies. long_description: In philosophy, the "state of nature" is the hypothetical way of life that existed before humans organized themselves into societies. In his 1651 work *Leviathan*, English philosopher Thomas Hobbes described man's life in this state as "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short". Hobbes believed natural man to be in constant motion, concerned primarily (or perhaps even only) with the satisfaction of their selfish desires, ever engaged in "the war of all against all". More than a century later, the French philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau argued, in contrast, that the state of nature is one of peace, freedom, and cooperation. War, he believed, did not exist until *after* societies, states, and all the rest of it came along. These contrasting beliefs about the basic nature of man - as basically (albeit simplistically) "good" or "evil" - has permeated philosophical and political discussions from antiquity to the present. What do you think man in his true "state of nature" is really like? And what does your answer mean for our understanding of society, law, and political power?

long_description:
In these turbulent times, it is crucial that we develop peaceful minds to enable the emergence of a more harmonious world. The format of this class was designed by Venerable Geshe Kelsang Gyatso Rinpoche so that people have a special method to create the causes for world peace.
Classes include a short teaching and advice for life, two guided meditations, and inspiring prayers for world peace.
After the class, join us for a pancake breakfast, coffee, tea and other delicious treats! Feel free to browse our bookstore for unique items.
Everyone is welcome.

Advice from Venerable Geshe Kelsang Gyatso, 2001
“World peace is very important; we cannot ignore this now. Once something happens, it will be too late. This world is now, as you know, very delicate, very fragile, and very sensitive. It is almost as delicate as the life of a single person; the world situation is so delicate. This is because there are so many disagreements. Political leaders are ready to fight; everybody is preparing weapons ready to fight, and are challenging each other. So we religious practitioners need to offer prayers because prayers are very powerful. This is because of our pure motivation, the powerful words of the prayers themselves, and especially at such times enlightened beings will bestow their blessings upon us, our environment and other living beings. So we should pray for world peace. We have had two world wars. If there is a third world war this will almost destroy the world because every country has very powerful weapons, and it is very easy to destroy the world. So I would like to suggest that every center organizes prayers for world peace at any time when local people can gather and pray for world peace.”

**Cost**
This event is free, you are welcome to make a donation.

long_description:
The Murfreesboro, TN Recovering From Religion support group will meet the third Sunday of every month at 3:00pm at the Technology Engagement Center, barring inclement weather or the date falls on a holiday. Attendees can remain anonymous if they so choose and are not required to tell their story if they do not wish to, but everyone will be welcomed to do so.

The primary focus of a Recovering From Religion support group is to provide ongoing and personal support to individuals as they let go of their religious beliefs. This transitional period is an ongoing process that can result in a range of emotions, as well as a ripple effect of consequences throughout an individual’s life. As such, the support meetings are safe and anonymous places to express these doubts, fears, and experiences without biased feedback or proselytizing.

We are here to help each other through this journey.

There is no cost to attend this support group but, if you feel so inclined, donations can be made at www.recoveringfromreligion.org/donate

RfR has an immense collection of well-curated resources available as you go through your journey. The page includes resources for mental and physical crises, working with relationships, for issues stemming from specific religions, coming out stories, and much more. Head to www.recoveringfromreligion.org/resources for these helpful resources.

If you find you need to talk with someone before the meeting date, RfR has a hotline and online chat for that express purpose. Call (844) 368-2848 to speak with someone or go to www.recoveringfromreligion.org to chat online.

If you are in need of professional help, we can offer the Secular Therapy Project to provide options to connect with a professional therapist. All therapists have been thoroughly vetted by our organization and offer only evidence-based and non-religious treatment. Connect with them at www.seculartherapy.org.

long_description:
**About our local meeting:**

The Mississippi Gulf Coast Recovering from Religion Support Group meets in person on the third Sunday of each month (except some holidays) at the Cat Island Coffeehouse Gulfport, 360 Courthouse Rd C, Gulfport, MS 39507. There is lot parking and the building is accessible to those with mobility impairments.

**\*\*\*PLEASE NOTE:\*\*\***
RSVP is **highly encouraged** to ensure adequate spacing and also to notify attendees of any last-minute changes, such as inclement weather.

Agenda:

* Opening announcements
* Introductions (You do not have to speak or give a real name)
* General discussion on topics related to religious recovery, doubt, or non-belief. We offer peer support and suggest resources as needed. **No preaching or proselytizing allowed**.
* Closing announcements including information and resources of interest, followed by optional social hangout

**What Recovering from Religion Is About:**

Do you doubt your beliefs? Have questions about changing or leaving your faith?

You are not alone—and we are here to help.

Recovering from Religion (RfR) exists to provide ongoing, personal support for individuals who are examining, changing, or choosing to let go of their religious beliefs. We are **not** here to deconvert anyone or tell you what to believe. We **are** here to offer understanding, support, and healing during what can often be a challenging and emotional transitional period.

This kind of transition can bring a wide range of feelings and may have a ripple effect across many areas of life. RfR Support Group meetings are designed to be **safe, anonymous spaces** where you can openly share doubts, fears, and experiences—without judgment, proselytizing, or biased feedback.

If you need someone to talk to before your meeting date, RfR offers both a hotline and an online chat for immediate support.
Call **(844) 368-2848** or visit **[www.recoveringfromreligion.org](http://www.recoveringfromreligion.org/)** to chat online.

description: Temple of Echoes: Sound Ceremony in the Cave of the Winds
long_description:
Dive into mystical vibes and let the cave’s natural echoes take you on a unique sound journey you won’t forget.

About this Event

On Sunday, August 16, 2026, at 7:30 pm, we gather for a two‑hour sacred sound ceremony within the ancient, living womb of Cave of the Winds. Cradled by stone and silence, this immersive experience invites you to step out of ordinary time and into a deep, ceremonial journey of remembrance, healing, and connection.
In this sanctified space, we will open with grounding, breath, and intention—crossing the threshold together as we honor the cave, the land, and the unseen allies that support our healing. You are invited to bring your prayers, your questions, your grief, your gratitude, and your quiet hopes, and offer them into the field of sound.
You will then be guided to rest comfortably as waves of sound gently move through and around you. A living tapestry of bells, crystal bowls, Tibetan bowls, gongs, chimes, drums, rattles, and flute will carry you inward, inviting your nervous system to soften, your mind to quiet, and your heart to open. Each tone, each vibration, is offered as medicine—to help you release what no longer serves and reconnect with the deeper wisdom of your body and spirit.

What to Expect from a Sound HealingDuring this sound healing journey, you will be lying down or seated in a relaxed position while the sounds and vibrations move through the cave and through your body. You may experience:
Deep physical relaxation as your body lets go of held tensionA quieter mind and a sense of spaciousness or stillness withinEmotional release, insights, or images rising from your inner landscapeGentle, energetic realignments, tingling sensations, or a feeling of lightnessEveryone’s experience is unique—there is no “right” way to receive. You are invited simply to notice, breathe, and allow.

Benefits and PurposeThis ceremony is designed to support you in:
Calming the nervous system and easing stress, overwhelm, and fatigueSupporting

description: A FREE outdoor yoga exploring  clarity, awareness and perspective through movement and breath. Open to all levels.
long_description:
A FREE outdoor yoga exploring clarity, awareness and perspective through movement and breath. Open to all levels.

About this Event

Expand & Embody is a FREE outdoor yoga series rooted in the belief that yoga isn’t just something we do on the mat. It’s a practice that helps us move through life with greater awareness, resilience, and ease.

Each class explores a different theme through intentional movement, breath, and reflection, creating space to strengthen both the body and the nervous system. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or have an established practice, you’ll be guided through an experience designed to leave you feeling more grounded, more present, and more capable of meeting life beyond the mat.

Class 6: Seeing (Third Eye Chakra)
Our sixth class explores the Third Eye Chakra, the energy center associated with awareness, intuition, and perspective. While clarity is often thought of as having all the answers, it begins with learning to observe ourselves with curiosity rather than judgment. Through intentional movement, breath, and mindful awareness, we’ll explore what it means to quiet the noise, recognize our patterns, and create space for greater clarity and insight.

organizer: Narrative Reflections:  Philosophy in Literature & Film
long_description:
Aristotle has been called "the First Teacher" by the Islamic philosophical tradition, "the Philosopher" by Thomas Aquinas, "the Colt" by his teacher Plato, and, much later, "the first mistake in Western philosophy" by Gilles Deleuze. Love him or hate him, his influence on philosophy and grasp on the development of Western thought is undeniable. For nearly two thousand years, his works shaped discussions of logic, ethics, politics, metaphysics, science, and theology.

Born in 384 BCE, Aristotle studied for twenty years at Plato's Academy before founding his own school, the Lyceum. He later served as tutor to Alexander the Great, whose conquests helped bring new knowledge of the natural world back to Greece. Although not a physician himself, Aristotle's emphasis on observation and classification profoundly influenced biology and medicine for centuries. He helped expand the work of Hippocrates and was a major influence on Galen.

Join us as we explore the life, ideas, and Philosophy of this amazing thinker. All are welcome, and no reading is required!

Take a break from the noise and join us for a refreshing hour of yoga in one of Arlington’s most beautiful outdoor spaces.

long_description:
### **🔥 Sunday Fire Circle — Queen's Beach Park (by Barefoot Beach Cafe)**

**Always free. Always open to watchers. No pressure, no cost — just come.**
End your weekend the way it deserves to end. We gather on the grass at Queen's Beach Park, right by Barefoot Beach Cafe, where the sun sets behind Waikiki and the ocean keeps time. Grab a coffee or a bite from Barefoot, find a soft patch of grass, and settle in.
This is O'ahu's cross-disciplinary movement arts community — fire dancers, poets, musicians, DJs, yogis, holistic facilitators, and friends. Come spin. Come share a piece. Come stretch, drum, sing, or just witness the circle come alive against the dusk.

**The Flow of the Night**

* **One hour before sunset** — Classes & skill shares. Beginner-friendly intros to poi, staff, fans, and safe spinning. Props to borrow, teachers ready.
* **Sunset** — The circle opens. Fire goes up, music comes on, the night begins. If you aren't spinning fire you are encouraged to dance to the music regardless!
* **9 PM** — Last burn. We pack out together.

**What to Bring (if you're spinning)**

* Natural fiber clothing (cotton or wool — no synthetics near flame)
* Water + a layer for after dark
* Your prop, instrument, mic, or mat
* A small light for setup and breakdown

**Just watching?** Bring yourself. Maybe a blanket. That's it.
**Before You Spin: Sign the Waiver**
Anyone stepping into the circle to spin needs to complete our waiver. Two minutes, online: **[https://www.trialbyfire.community/fire-circle](https://www.trialbyfire.community/fire-circle)**
**Community Guidelines**

* **Consent first** — ask before you touch, photograph, or enter someone's space.
* **Substance-free** — Strictly no alcohol, no cocaine, no ketamine.
* **The circle is working space** — stay outside the perimeter unless you're spinning, fueling, or on safety.
* **Respect the fuel, props, and people.**
* **Leave it better than you found it.**

Bringing together live music, dance, visual art, and storytelling, this immersive program celebrates the power of the arts to spark curiosity, deepen our connection with the natural world, and invite us to see it through fresh eyes. Experience how music, movement, visual art, and community come together to celebrate the wonder of the natural world.
Violinist Iggy Jang, harpist Megan Conley, and Ballet Hawaiʻi dancer Aria Kaneshiga present a 25-minute performance featuring music by Camille Saint-Saëns and Stephanie Ann Boyd, inspired by whales, butterflies, and kāhuli (Hawaiian land snails). Through expressive music and movement, audiences of all ages are invited on a journey of creativity, curiosity, and wonder.
**Performances:** At 11am and 12pm.
**Make puppets:** From 10am to 2pm visitors are invited to participate in a puppet-making activity led by local artist Danica Rosengren, inspired by the featured animals and themes of the performance.
**See a film:** Continue the experience with a special free film screening of *Ocean with David Attenborough* in Doris Duke Theatre at 2pm, followed by a short talk story featuring local conservation leaders of Hawaiʻi's marine life, as well as meaningful ways we can all help protect and preserve it.

History: Gabriele Rausse is widely recognized as the "Father of the Modern Virginia Wine Industry". Originally from Valdagno, Italy, he moved to Virginia in 1976. Brought over by Italian winemaker Gianni Zonin, Rausse successfully pioneered the cultivation of European Vitis vinifera grapes at Barboursville Vineyards. In 1997, he established his own boutique winery in Albemarle County. Today, alongside his sons Peter and Tim, he produces small-batch, traditionally crafted wines using varietals like Nebbiolo, Grüner Veltliner, and Chasselas Doré.

long_description:
* **YOGA AT THE BLUFFS**
**🙏💚🙏**

Aging is often spoken of as something to resist, yet yoga invites us to meet it differently. Through steady breath, mindful movement, and quiet attention, the practice reminds us that the body is always changing, yet still capable of strength, balance, and renewal.

Modern research is beginning to affirm what practitioners have long sensed through experience. Studies suggest that regular yoga practice may support mobility and balance, nurture emotional well-being, and even influence the body at the cellular level—supporting processes related to cellular health and renewal as we age.
Perhaps this is yoga’s quiet wisdom: aging is not something we must fight, but something we can meet with awareness, compassion, and care. In this way, the practice becomes more than exercise—it becomes a gentle companion for living each season of life with presence, resilience, radiance, , and grace.
**Yoga for Healthy Aging: Science or Hype?**
**Click link below to read statistical and significant research on aging benefits of yoga practice:**
**[https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8341166/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8341166/)**

All Osher Movement Classes are facilitated by an instructor with experience and specific training working with participants with chronic pain and conditions.

Modifications available if support of a chair or the wall is needed. M2 classes are suitable for those comfortable moving independently.

long_description:
**THE GREAT MINGLE**
**Come Curious. Who Will You Meet?**

Looking to meet new people beyond your usual circle?

Join Tribe of One Love for **The Great Mingle**, a fun and intentionally structured social experience designed to help you connect with people you may never have met otherwise.
Many social events naturally lead us to spend time with the people we already know. ***The Great Mingle is different.***

Using a format we call **The Social Shuffle**, we'll guide participants through a series of small-group conversations designed to make meeting new people easy, comfortable, and engaging.

No awkward networking. No pressure. Just meaningful conversations with interesting humans.

Whether you're new to the community or a long-time member, you'll have the opportunity to meet a variety of people, hear their stories, share your own, and leave feeling more connected than when you arrived.

**Shared Intention**
To create opportunities for genuine human connection by stepping beyond our familiar circles, approaching one another with curiosity, and recognizing that every person carries a unique story worth discovering. And while our gatherings give us a place to start, Tribe of One Love hopes the magic doesn’t end there—may the conversations, friendships, and unexpected sparks continue to grow naturally long after the event lights dim.

long_description:
**YOGA AT THE BLUFFS**
**INTEGRATIVE HEALT AND WELLNESS**
**FOR SUCCESFUL AGING**

As there is a science and technology to create external well-being, there is a whole dimension since and technology for inner well-being - and that is yoga! Increase your vitality, resiliency, physical strength and flexibility, energy, stabilize your mind, calm your emotions and find joy in your life. Yoga practice will help you manage your energy, sleep better, eat better, have better relationships and help you to feel more ease and happiness in your life. This is the promise of yoga.

My classes are held every Monday and Wednesday mornings in Eastbluff, Newport Beach, at 10am-11:15am. They are donation based. Classes are gentle and appropriate for the perfect beginner, or strong practitioner.

Classes are breath centric, and adapted to your needs, age, lifestyle, and condition. I am a yoga teacher and yoga therapist certified through International Association of Yoga Therapy. I teach all ages but partiucaly focus on seniors (ages 55-105). Poses are adapted for your individual need. We practice poses to increase strength, flexibility, ROM, balance, focus, and concentration. The breath work increases vitality and health of all your systems; cardiovascular, respiratory, circulatory, immune, and digestive. Class is followed by meditation to help stabilize the mind and emotions, and bring one to state of inner light and joy.

Please bring a mat, a smile, and an open curious mind. You deserve to be healthy, happy, and whole. An added benefit of these classes is that you will meet some very nice people.

If interested you can email me at janet@heartofyoga.com or respond on meetup.

May you be happy and well!

Janet Marshall
E-RYT -500
IAYT

long_description:
I have been studying, training and teaching yoga for over 25 years. I want to help serve others by sharing this powerful tradition. I work with seniors as well as teenagers. I am a Yoga Teacher E-RYT500 as well as trained Yoga Therapist with the International Association of Yoga Therapy.
I was planning on going back to school to get a PhD in Yoga Science and Ayurveda, but my teacher told me that if I needed to start teaching. He said that in this tradition, if you don't teach what you have learned in yoga to others, it is considered stealing.
So, I have been sharing and teaching ever since now for many years. I have loads of information and can share a multitude of practices to help with any specific need or condition (physical, physiological, mental/ emotional/ spiritual ).
The goal of yoga is to reduce suffering on all levels (physical, energetic, mental/emotional, find joy, and BECOME FREE! SPEAKING OF FREE, I offer 4 free community yoga classes a week each Monday and Wednesday for Eastbluff Community. Please consider joining a class or two, meet your neighbors, have some fun, and increase your longevity, health span, and overall wellness and connect to the joy that resides within your heart ❤️. For more details you can contact me here or email me at janet@heartofyoga.com

long_description:
**Classes are every Monday and Wednesday Mornings. Regular mat class from 10am-11:15am, and Chair Yoga from 12pm-1pm.**
**Classes are gentle and breath centric. Poses are adapted to meet your needs. Regardless of your age, health, condition, if you can breath you can do yoga!! Increase your strength, flexibility, balance, energy, mental focus, and overall feelings of well-being and joy! Classes are free or donation based. Join the community, meet new connections while growing younger. Please RSVP or email me at janet@atheartofyoga,com for more details.**

### **Yoga is a journey. We can take that journey together, and it can be your guide for life. Yoga is NOT an aesthetic practice of aspiration. It is a practice to reclaim your joy and develop your physical and mental resilience.**

### **Let 2023 be the year to let go of old patterns that hold you back from wellness, and make space for what is most precious; wellness in body, mind, heart, soul, and the abundance of joy and friendships.**

### **The ancient practices of yoga and meditation cultivates wisdom and wellness and a caravan in which we move through all of life's joys and struggles. Yoga is the most ancient, deepest, and potent of medicines.**

### **And the good news is that ANYONE can practice yoga. If you are breathing. ..You can do yoga! Regular practice promises the reduction of suffering (Dukha) and brings health to body, peace to your heart, and joy in heart.**

### **As the great Sri K Patabhi Jois says "Practice and all is coming" The ancient practices of yoga and meditation cultivates wisdom and wellness and a caravan in which we move through all of life's joys and struggles.**

### **It is a true joy to share the teachings of yoga. Over the years I have witnesses so much healing, joy, in my students, as well as the friendships and connections made.**

### **Wishing you an abundance of health, courage, inspiration and blessings in the year ahead!**

### **Namaste🙏,**

### **Janet Marshall**

title: Mindfulness Mondays: Breathwork, Kirtan & SoundBath
description: An evening of pranayama, collective chanting of mantras and mindfulness meditation.
long_description:
An evening of pranayama, collective chanting of mantras and mindfulness meditation.

About this Event

Escape the summer rush and step into a space of profound presence. Join us for a unique, large-scale community gathering dedicated to deep mindfulness, sacred sound, and inner peace.
​Led by Bhakti Yogis, this evening is an immersive journey through three distinct stages of ancient meditation practices designed to quiet the mind and open the heart.
​The Flow of the Evening:
​Pranayama (Breathwork): We will begin by calming the nervous system with restorative, grounding breathing techniques to release the stress of the day and center our awareness.
​Kirtan (Sacred Sound): Transitioning from breath to sound, we will experience the vibrant, heart-opening practice of kirtan—collective, call-and-response musical chanting that naturally uplifts the room's energy.
​Japa Meditation: To close the evening, we will channel that collective energy inward, concluding with a focused, quiet japa meditation practice to experience profound stillness and deep personal clarity.
​Whether you are a seasoned practitioner or exploring these practices for the very first time, this evening offers a powerful collective environment to reset, ground, and connect.
​Event Details:
​Date & Time: Monday at 7:00 PM (Doors open at 6:45 PM; the practice begins promptly at 7:00 PM)
​What to bring: Bring your water and Comfortable clothing. Cushions/mats are provided at the venue, but feel free to bring your own personal cushion for maximum comfort.

Also check out other Health & Wellness events in Atlanta, Bhajan jamming events in Atlanta.

“The Master Mind principle: Two or more people actively engaged in the pursuit of a definite purpose with a positive mental attitude, constitute an unbeatable force.”

— Napoleon Hill

Empire Builders Mastermind (Growth Strategies) group is hosted by International Success Coach Misty Rose Gold. We come together in the true mastermind fashion talked about in Napoleon Hill's book Think And Grow Rich. We support each other through challenges that come as you build your empire. Knowing that you are not alone is half the battle. When challenges arise we use our collective knowledge to create a solution. The commitment and accountability of the group is a game changer for those looking for a unique and proven experience to grow their empire.

If you have a skill set that can add value to our mastermind, come and visit us. We would love to meet you! One visit allowed per person. If you love us we will take a vote. If voted in you will become a valuable member of a game changing group.

If you are looking for a traditional networking group please move on. Do we network in the mastermind group? Yes, it naturally takes place if someone is in need of something specific. Otherwise we are there to learn, grow, support, and crush our goals.

Each week, Misty presents a topic that covers the fundamentals of building a successful empire with integrity. Such as, "What gives your empire credibility?" If you are messy and run over people to get ahead don't bother. We will vote you out anyway. Integrity is the core value of our mastermind group. If you believe in doing business with integrity bring it! Come check us out. Your next level awaits!

To learn more about Misty, please visit her website at www.mistyrosegold.com. You can listen to Wealthy Mind podcast on all platforms. It'll give you an instant boost of motivation!

long_description:
Tech Talk:
**What Makes a Good Host: The Art and Science of Choosing a Website Platform in an AI Future**

We are bringing back our tech talks. This next session with be with Kate Kight

**Who is Kate:**
Kate is a creative technologist who believes in the power of design to solve problems and bring people together. From national brand identities to customized CRMs for local nonprofits, Kate creates scalable solutions designed to look good and do good.

**What to expect:**
A few years ago, it was almost impossible to believe the era of drag-and-drop websites would ever come to an end. But as major platforms wall in their tech stacks, hike prices, and cram in AI features to justify the cost, it’s time to explore alternatives. While AI can't replace human strategy, it can unlock cheaper, more scalable web hosting options with fewer tradeoffs.
Drawing on her expertise in crafting scrappy solutions for growing startups, Kate will share hands-on frameworks for selecting the right website builder, knowing when to hire a specialist (and whether you need a designer, developer, or business strategist), and scaling sustainably. You’ll walk away with actionable tools to avoid tech debt and build a digital foundation that grows with your business.

A FREE outdoor yoga exploring presence, perspective and purpose through movement and breath. Open to all levels.

About this Event

Expand & Embody is a FREE outdoor yoga series rooted in the belief that yoga isn’t just something we do on the mat. It’s a practice that helps us move through life with greater awareness, resilience, and ease.

Each class explores a different theme through intentional movement, breath, and reflection, creating space to strengthen both the body and the nervous system. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or have an established practice, you’ll be guided through an experience designed to leave you feeling more grounded, more present, and more capable of meeting life beyond the mat.

Class 7: Expanding (Crown Chakra)
Our seventh class explores the Crown Chakra, the energy center associated with awareness, purpose, and connection. While expansion is often thought of as reaching for something beyond ourselves, it begins by recognizing that we are already connected - to ourselves, to one another, and to the world around us. Through intentional movement, breath, and mindful awareness, we’ll explore what it means to create space for greater presence, perspective, and possibility.

long_description:
**ABOUT THE THIRD OPTION PROGRAM**

The Third Option is a group program to build better relationships. It is designed for all people and can be used as enrichment for healthy couples who want to enhance their relationship, or as crisis intervention for couples who are separated or considering divorce.

This class combines skill-building workshops with sharing from couples that have “been there”, and a support group component. The atmosphere is warm and caring.

**WHAT IS “THE THIRD OPTION?”**

For a couple who is struggling, Option 1 is to stay miserable in an unhappy relationship, and Option 2 is to get out – divorce. “The Third Option” is to learn the skills needed to have a happy and healthy relationship. If even one partner wants to work at the relationship, they can come alone, and the relationship will benefit. It's better yet if both partners attend.

**WHEN DO THE CLASSES OCCUR?**

This ongoing class meets every Tuesday evening from 6:30 to 8:30pm. The Third Option operates on a 14 week cycle that restarts again after the last week, so it’s continuous. This means it is OK to join at any time.

There is no charge to attend the first two weeks; after that there is a suggested donation of $10 per person, per week (if finances are a problem, come anyway! No one is ever turned away by lack of funds). There's no need to sign up ahead of time, and the group keeps confidentiality about who attends and what is shared.

**WHERE DO THE CLASSES MEET?**

long_description:
Come to receive a session of Light Energy. Sessions are 15-60 minutes depending on your schedule and preference. There is no cost, but spiritual offerings to the Sukyo Mahikari (http://sukyomahikari.org/) organization are welcomed.

Why receive Light?

Various spiritual principles underlie the natural world. Sometimes it is easy to practice the universal principles, but sometimes even people who want to live in harmony with their innate spirituality encounter situations where they do not know how to apply the universal principles. For example, people may find themselves in a job or relationship that makes them unhappy or which hinders them from accomplishing their goals. When tools for spiritual growth are practiced together with experiencing light energy, people can more quickly attain personal growth and help make the world a better place.

What is Light?

Energy that purifies the spiritual aspect of people and all things. Light can be radiated to anything – food, animals, plants, homes, workplaces, cars, and so on. By purifying their surroundings with this energy, many people notice that their surroundings become more pleasant and often appear brighter. This helps everyone around them gradually become more connected with their spirituality and to start to think more about how to live in harmony with their fellow human beings and the environment.

Where can you read more about it?

"True Light: Ordinary People on the Extraordinary Spiritual Path of Sukyo Mahikari" was recently published.

description:

Using a real-world example of an AI-enabled application built around human communication and personalization, this session explores what happens when technology is designed to adapt to people instead of forcing people to adapt to the technology. The idea for Selvo was inspired by her brother
organizer: Women in Technology of the Heartland
long_description:
RSVP on Meetup and join us to hear Emily Kenney, Data Scientist and founder of Selvo, discuss how AI is reshaping software engineering, product design, and the skills technical teams need to stay relevant.

Using a real-world example of an AI-enabled application built around human communication and personalization, this session explores what happens when technology is designed to adapt to people instead of forcing people to adapt to the technology. The idea for Selvo was inspired by her brother Lucas’s experience losing his ability to speak, read, and write, which led Emily to imagine a more personalized communication tool.

Attendees will learn about the changing role of technical teams in an AI-native world, including product judgment, experimentation, data quality, evaluation, responsible AI, accessibility and cross-functional collaboration. Emily will also explore why the future of software should be centered on human agency, helping more people communicate, create, participate, and be understood.

**About Our Speaker**
Emily Kenney is the Senior Director of AI Delivery for The Standard and an instructor at the Omaha Data Science Academy. She is also the founder and CEO of Selvo, a personalized communication companion.

She holds a B.S. in Bioinformatics from the University of Nebraska at Omaha, where she was a NASA Student Fellowship recipient, and an M.I.D.S. from UC Berkeley.

**Special Thanks**
Thank you to the [Omaha Data Science Academy](https://canlearnsmart.com/) for sponsoring this event, to [The Reserves Network](https://www.trnstaffing.com/) for hosting, and to the [Nebraska Tech Collaborative](https://aksarben.org/ntc/) for being our 2026 sponsor!

5:00 – 5:30 Networking, Food and Drinks
5:30 – 5:40 Announcements

organizer: A Cappella Singers and Vocalists of Upstate NY
long_description:
Men of the New York State Capital District with a desire to sing in an accomplished chorus are invited to join the chorus and take advantage of our excellent leadership and instruction. The Electric City Chorus is a men’s a cappella vocal music group singing in the Barbershop Style. We strive to sing at the highest quality, to entertain, and to experience great fellowship and enjoyment.

You do not have to be a great singer; you just need to be a guy who likes to sing, and willing to learn. You do not have to be able to sing your part alone; you will be singing with the chorus. If you have ever sung in the shower or found yourself singing along with the music on the radio, chances are you will enjoy singing with us. If you are a little nervous about the whole idea, bring a friend along for moral (and vocal) support!

Visit one of our rehearsals and check us out. You won't be pressured to join, but you will have a lot of fun singing with us.

The ECC meets every Tuesday at 7:00 PM at Schenectady Light Opera's Performing Arts Center (enter at 418 Liberty Street in Schenectady), unless we are out singing somewhere in the community. For more information email: manager@electriccitychorus.net; visit our website at: https://www.electriccitychorus.net/, or see us on Facebook, at: https://www.facebook.com/ElectricCityChorus/

The Electric City Chorus is a member of the international barbershop organization, the Barbershop Harmony Society, in the Northeast District (NED).

The ECC sings at many community venues in all seasons of the year. In addition, the chorus periodically competes and sings with other choruses in the northeast section of the United States and eastern Canada.

long_description:
**Agenda**

* 5:30 - 6:30pm Networking
* 6:30 - 7:30pm Presentation
* 7:30 - 7:45pm Closing

**Abstract**
So you push a Kubernetes Helm chart in your Visual Studio Code IDE from your local to a Git branch and kickoff the pipeline in Harness for the changes to be deployed to a container. You'd then have to go to OCP (or your cloud provider of choice), open stateful sets, pod logs to how the deployment is going on. What if you could see all that right where you pushed your code? You could be coding in your IDE all the while seeing the status of your pods.

This talk presents a practical architecture for exposing operational capabilities through MCP-style servers (Model Context Protocol) so developers can interact with OpenShift resources directly from their local development environment. Instead of treating the IDE as only a coding surface, we turn it into a controlled entry point for runtime diagnostics such as pod log retrieval, namespace-aware querying, rollout inspection, and incident triage.

I will also be posting the link to my MCP server that anybody can use and customize to their needs!

**Bio**
Vineel Arekapudi works at the intersection of large-scale data engineering, cloud platforms, and applied AI. He currently builds and leads modern data platforms at a major U.S. bank, where he designs lakehouse and streaming architectures that operate at multi-billion-record scale across cloud environments.

His background spans the full evolution of enterprise data systems—from mainframe and Teradata warehouses to cloud-native lakehouses built on Spark, Iceberg, Kafka, and Kubernetes. Over the past decade, his work has focused on building production-grade data platforms, including high-throughput ingestion pipelines, real-time analytics systems, and ML-ready data infrastructure used by data scientists, analysts, and AI teams.

long_description:
**YOGA AT THE BLUFFS**
**INTEGRATIVE HEALT AND WELLNESS**
**FOR SUCCESFUL AGING**
FREE YOGA CLASSES !

Just as there is a science and technology to create external well-being, there is a whole dimension since and technology for inner well-being - and that is yoga!

Increase your vitality, resiliency, physical strength and flexibility, energy, stabilize your mind, calm your emotions and find joy in your life. Yoga practice will help you manage your energy, sleep better, eat better, have better relationships and help you to feel more ease and happiness in your life. This is the promise of yoga.

My classes are held every Monday and Wednesday mornings in Newport Beach at Eastbluff Clubhouse: 2490 Vista del Oro. Class times are from 10am-11:20am. Classes are gentle and appropriate for the perfect beginner, or strong practitioner, and FREE or donation based!

Classes are breath centric, and adapted to your needs, age, lifestyle, and condition. I am a yoga teacher and yoga therapist certified through International Association of Yoga Therapy. I trained for over 20 years in several traditions but teach in the Viniyoga tradition of Krishnamacharya. I teach all ages but my particular focus in teaching seniors (ages 55-105).

Poses are adapted for your individual need. We practice poses to increase strength, flexibility, ROM, balance, focus, and concentration. The breath work increases vitality and health of all your systems; cardiovascular, respiratory, circulatory, immune, and digestive. Class is followed by meditation to help stabilize the mind and emotions, and bring one to state of inner light and joy.

Please bring a mat, a smile, and an open curious mind. You deserve to be healthy, happy, and whole, and the practices of yoga guide you towards better overall health and wellbeing. An added benefit of these classes is that you will meet some very nice people.

If interested you can email me at janet@heartofyoga.com or respond on meetup.

May you be happy and well!
Janet M
