long_description:
This is a casual monthly book club in which we discuss a book we've read on a southwest history topic. In July, we'll discuss *Revolt at Taos: The New Mexican and Indian Insurrection of 1847* by James A. Crutchfield.

Description:
On the morning of January 19, 1847, Charles Bent, the newly appointed governor of the American-claimed territory of New Mexico, was savagely killed at his home in Don Fernando de Taos, a small, remote town located north of Santa Fe. Those responsible for Bent’s murder were New Mexican settlers and Indians from nearby Taos Pueblo who refused to recognize the United States occupation. With emotions rubbed raw, the natives continued their bloodbath until five more leading citizens were massacred in Taos. During the ensuing months, American civilians and soldiers, along with scores of New Mexicans and Taos Indians, were killed and wounded throughout the region. Less than a month following Bent’s murder, in a two-day battle, volunteer and regular elements of an American army under the command of Colonel Sterling Price emerged victorious after bombarding the insurrectionists at their refuge in the church at Taos Pueblo. Surviving participants in the earlier Taos murders were arrested, tried in American-dominated courts, and, within weeks, hanged for their actions. The murder of Bent and the others at Taos and the subsequent trials and executions brought with them misunderstanding, controversy, mistrust, and recrimination on both sides of the issue. The events also subjected President James K. Polk’s administration to censure over what some critics believed was an overextension of presidential authority in claiming New Mexico as a territory.
In *Revolt at Taos: The New Mexican and Indian Insurrection of 1847*, writer and historian James A. Crutchfield explores the fast-moving events surrounding the bloody revolt which left native inhabitants of New Mexico wondering how their neighbors and kinsmen could be legally tried, found guilty, and executed

This is a talk for anyone serious about doing meaningful creative work. Whether you’re just starting out or years into your career, expect a perspective check and a few uncomfortable truths that will make you better.

long_description:
We'll start promptly at 5:30 with a walk/easy hike in a very beautiful park then gather at 6:45 for a discussion on the book **Alias Grace** by Margaret Atwood. **Bring a chair. Rainy weather will change place and time so keep an eye out for updates if it's a rainy day.**

This book takes us back in time and into the life and mind of one of the most enigmatic and notorious women of the nineteenth century. Grace Marks has been convicted for her involvement in the vicious murders of her employer, the wealthy Thomas Kinnear, and of Nancy Montgomery, his housekeeper and mistress. Some believe Grace is innocent; others think her evil or insane. Now serving a life sentence after a stint in Toronto's lunatic asylum, Grace herself claims to have no memory of the murders.

Dr. Simon Jordan, an up-and-coming expert in the burgeoning field of mental illness, is engaged by a group of reformers and spiritualists who seek a pardon for Grace. He listens to her story, from her family's difficult passage out of Ireland into Canada, to her time as a maid in Thomas Kinnear's household. As he brings Grace closer and closer to the day she cannot remember, he hears of the turbulent relationship between Kinnear and Nancy Montgomery, and of the alarming behavior of Grace's fellow servant, James McDermott. Jordan is drawn to Grace, but he is also baffled by her. What will he find in attempting to unlock her memories? Is Grace a female fiend, a bloodthirsty femme fatale? Or is she a victim of circumstances?

title: Smarter Water Systems Through Artificial Intelligence Models
description: The conversation around AI is understandably dominated by large language models, yet the computational cost and expertise required to deploy them remains out of reach for most water engineering organizations — even as sensor and telemetry data grows faster than engineers can interpret it. This presentation explores a practical intermediate path: smaller, first-principles-aligned AI models paired with agentic workflow orchestration that lower the barrier to entry while preserving interpretability
long_description:
The conversation around AI is understandably dominated by large language models, yet the computational cost and expertise required to deploy them remains out of reach for most water engineering organizations — even as sensor and telemetry data grows faster than engineers can interpret it. This presentation explores a practical intermediate path: smaller, first-principles-aligned AI models paired with agentic workflow orchestration that lower the barrier to entry while preserving interpretability and deployability. Three applied examples spanning force main monitoring, treatment optimization, and collection system planning and control ground the discussion, illustrating how embedding domain physics into smaller models can improve reliability under uncertain climate and growth conditions. Together, they offer a concrete and auditable bridge toward more sophisticated AI integration in water systems.

Caleb Buahin is a hydroinformatics engineer with over 15 years of experience in engineering consulting and applied research. His work advances integrated modeling frameworks and digital technologies for cost-effective and resilient water systems. He has applied these frameworks to a range of water systems, including large lake/reservoir–river systems, stormwater and wastewater collection systems, and drinking water distribution networks. Caleb is currently a lead data scientist at Hazen and Sawyer, where he fuses traditional engineering methods with emerging AI/ML techniques to help clients navigate the ongoing digital water transformation. Areas of concentration include long-term control and capital improvement planning, predictive maintenance, and digital twins for real-time control and operational decision support.

Session will take place 4-5pm, followed by networking 5-6pm. Refreshments will be provided. Meetups are hosted the third Wednesday of each month at Union Hall in OTR and feature subject matter experts and enthusiasts in the fields of data and analytics.

organizer: Travel and Culture Group in Omaha
long_description:
Denmark consistently rates as one of the happiest countries on Earth. Every element of their culture today is infused with this happiness, making it one of the safest, easiest places in the world to visit. Happiness, however, is serious business; from how they design their spaces to how they balance work and life, Danes try very hard to maintain a culture of happiness. In this talk by Adam Bierstedt (curator for the Museum of Danish America), come learn about Denmark, and how Danish happiness shapes the culture of Denmark today... including why Denmark is such a safe and welcoming place to visit, and how the Museum of Danish America brings Danish culture, history, design, and storytelling to life right here in the Iowa prairie!

He’ll also give us an inside look at the museum’s newest exhibits (such as Viking-mania!), including updates from behind the scenes. Plus the museum’s newest visitor favorite: a 25 foot tall Thomas Dambo troll! Thomas Dambo is the famous artist who's created more than 170 wooden troll sculptures across 17 countries, and now Iowa is home to one of them!

Come join us on Wednesday, August 19th at 6:30pm for an unforgettable evening with Adam!

**ABOUT OUR SPEAKER:** Adam Bierstedt is the Albert Ravenholt Curator of Danish American Culture. A Midwest native, he was introduced to Scandinavian culture through lefse, mostly. From 2017-2020, he lived in Iceland and Denmark, and has visited many times since. He has been with the Museum of Danish America since 2024, where he is the designer of all the museum’s exhibitions. Most recently, he opened *Vikingmania!* as a celebration of our modern obsession with all things Viking-themed.

Schedule:
6:30 PM: Social time – Grab a drink, mingle, and meet fellow travelers
7 PM: Presentation: Denmark & Museum of Danish America
8 PM-ish: Event finishes

long_description:
**Summary of the Presentation:**
In July 2026, an AI agent compromised Hugging Face's production infrastructure. It did not "go rogue," and that is precisely what should concern every security team. During an authorized OpenAI evaluation, the model was told to solve a security benchmark and pursued that objective relentlessly: it discovered a zero-day, escalated privileges, moved laterally, and chained stolen credentials into a remote-code-execution path no human had ever modeled. Each individual action looked valid; the danger emerged from their composition.
When an agent can assemble a path nobody modeled, prevention alone is a losing bet. The real question is not only how to control what an agent can access, but how to reverse what it does when controls fail.
That is where Rubrik is different: we assume agentic overreach will eventually slip through, and we let security teams rewind it, undoing an agent's destructive actions and restoring a trusted state.
As organizations race to deploy AI agents, controlling access is no longer enough. The Cloud Security Alliance has identified multiple challenges facing enterprises; this session focuses on three:

* **Visibility of AI Agents:** discovering and maintaining an accurate inventory of every agent, including shadow and unmanaged ones.
* **Over-Privileged Agents:** identifying agents that have accumulated permissions well beyond their intended function.
* **Governing Agent Behavior:** continuously ensuring agents act within their approved purpose over time.

We will show how Rubrik Agent Cloud and its Semantic AI Governance Engine (SAGE) address these challenges through continuous semantic understanding of agent identity, intent, permissions, and runtime behavior. SAGE reasons about what an action is actually trying to accomplish, translating natural-language policy into real-time allow or block decisions and catching anomalies no static rule anticipated.

long_description:
At this junction of time and political environment, it is easy to realize how much cultural diplomacy plays. This annual gala is magnifies the American and Rusian cultural relationships through entertainment and food. Exhibits, like a centennial time travel of Photojournalism to Cinematography (1914 - 2014). It is also decorated by the presence of The Ambassador of Russia to the USA.

Black Tie required.

This great bell was first cast in the 15th century. In the early 1600’s it was
recast to hang in the Kremlin’s “Ivan the Great Bell Tower.” It fell in a fire in the
mid-17th century. It was recast again only to suffer a similar fate. It was recast
a third time in 1735, and once again damaged by fire which caused an 11 ton
chunk to break away. The bell collapsed into its casting pit where it remained
for a century. Many efforts to excavate it were made, including Napoleon’s, who
wanted to take it as a trophy after occupying Moscow in 1812. The bell was
raised in 1836 and placed on a stone pedestal in the Kremlin. At over 200 tons,
it remains the largest in the world.
Photo: Gilbert H. Grosvenor, "Young Russia: The Land of Unlimited Possibilities."
National Geographic Magazine, November 1914.

long_description:
**The Art of Hands-On Adjustments & Assists**

Join us for an informative and experiential workshop designed for yoga teachers, teacher trainees, and dedicated students who wish to deepen their understanding of hands-on adjustments and assists. Rooted in the traditions of Astāṅga Yoga, skillful adjustments can help students experience greater alignment, stability, awareness, and ease within a posture while supporting the development of a safe and effective practice.

This workshop will explore the principles behind effective assisting, including proper body mechanics, communication, observation skills, and the distinction between adjusting, assisting, and supporting. Participants will learn how to assess individual needs, apply appropriate levels of pressure and guidance, and offer adjustments that enhance rather than force a posture.
We will work through a wide range of postures from the standing, seated, and reclining sequences, as well as techniques for supporting students in relaxation and Śavāsana. Emphasis will be placed on maintaining the integrity of the pose, honoring individual differences, and cultivating confidence and sensitivity as an assistant.
Whether you are a teacher looking to refine your hands-on skills or a student curious about the role of adjustments in yoga practice, this workshop will provide practical tools, hands-on experience, and a deeper appreciation for the art of assisting others on the yoga path.

\*Yoga Alliance YACEP accredited hours available

You will be asked to wear a hair net or you can bring a baseball cap or hat to manage your hair. You can also bring your own apron if you own one.

There is free street parking in the area, usually on the same street or the next block. It is also near CTA bus routes.

description:
This session is led by Lauren Stone, a founding member of Ladies that UX Atlanta and now one of the chapter's co-organizers. She is a Product Designer specializing in enterprise SaaS products with a decade of experience and a twice-certified OOUX strategist.

long_description:
This session is led by Lauren Stone, a founding member of Ladies that UX Atlanta and now one of the chapter's co-organizers. She is a Product Designer specializing in enterprise SaaS products with a decade of experience and a twice-certified OOUX strategist.

OOUX — the Object-Oriented UX methodology created by Sophia Prater — gives us a powerful, structured way to think about the objects in any system. In this workshop we're using that framework as our lens to explore the foundational discipline underneath it: Information Architecture.

*We're keeping it focused. Just nouns.*
You'll learn to:

* Forage for the core objects in any system
* Identify and classify what you find
* Organize those nouns into a hierarchy
* See how that structure maps directly to UI decisions

All experience levels welcome. Space is limited.

**Please connect with us on Google Groups at [https://groups.google.com/g/cinpa-security-sig](https://groups.google.com/g/cinpa-security-sig) to stay updated on notices.** (This [link](https://support.google.com/groups/answer/1067205) will explain how to join the group.)

You can also follow us on [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/search/results/all/?fetchDeterministicClustersOnly=true&heroEntityKey=urn%3Ali%3Aorganization%3A108011493&keywords=cinpa%20-%20security%20sig&origin=RICH_QUERY_TYPEAHEAD_HISTORY&position=0&searchId=53b240fd-c310-46a3-a243-9faa8c98a079&sid=zci&spellCorrectionEnabled=true).

The CiNPA Security SIG's monthly meeting format typically consists of one or two main monthly meeting topics featuring live presentations or demonstrations promoting open and interactive group discussions. Our focus is primarily on the technical aspects of InfoSec, but we occasionally touch on other areas of cybersecurity as well. Information security news, announcements, and round-table discussions follow our main meeting topics.

Attendee Benefits:

• Attendance qualifies for 2 hours of CPE or CEU credit towards certification renewals

• Maintaining awareness of new vulnerabilities and exploits

• Learning about the latest security tools, utilities, products, services, solutions, strategies, techniques, frameworks, and best practices

• Sharing of information regarding trends concerning enterprise systems and technology

• Hearing announcements of upcoming area security conferences and events

• Networking with peers in the local Information Security (InfoSec) community

long_description:
**Title:** Silicon Societies: What happens when millions of AI agents use the Internet alongside us?

**Abstract:** When OpenClaw came out in early 2026, one of the first things people did was upload these new agents into their own AI social network, and thus MoltBook was born. For many, this was their first exposure to how AI agents interact with each other on a large scale. Increasingly, interfaces are designed for agent-first interactions (such as, for example, ChatGPT allowing AI agents to buy things online), so we’ll have to reckon with a world increasingly designed for AI agents to talk to other AI agents. But what happens when everyone has their own personal AI agents, each with their own personality and preferences, and then those AI agents are set loose on the Internet? What happens when all these AI agents come together to make their own “AI societies” independent of ours? Do 1,000,000 AI agents make decisions and see the world the same way as 1,000,000 people? And what happens on online platforms when you don’t know whether the person you’re talking to is real or AI? Both academia and industry are designing AI simulations as a way of studying these questions and more. The study of AI agent simulation is relatively nascent, and in this talk I’ll share a few insights into how AI agent societies are emerging in the wild, what we can and can’t learn from simulating them at scale so far, why we should be cautious about assuming silicon societies would work the same way as ours, and what may remain uniquely human in an online world increasingly designed to be used by AI agents.

**Audience Takeaway:** We are building an internet where AI agents have their own social media feeds, pay for their own groceries, and confirm medical appointments for us, often working alongside us rather than just for us. We'll spend the first 45 minutes moving and breathing with the ocean, soulful beats, and our sweet community, and then transition to a 30 minute dance party at the ocean's edge 🌊✨

This all-levels creative vinyasa flow class moves through postures at a steady pace, cultivating a sense of connection within ourselves and our surroundings. The intention of this class is to create ease, joy, health and healing in heart, body and mind. With each class you will build strength, suppleness and flexibility.

Near the end of our practice we head down to the water’s edge for a dance party, inviting a playful and freeing aspect to your practice. You can expect an exquisitely curated soundtrack of music— from fun and familiar, booty-shakin beats, to soft, soulful tracks meant to soothe the heart, to other worldly sounds that are sure to inspire ecstatic expression— informing an ever-changing tapestry of movement and emotion.

With views of the Golden Gate Bridge, resting your eyes on the waves as you practice, and watching birds soar above, curated music and our incredible community - it’s truly a magical experience to be immersed in.

About your teacher, Kirin:
My classes are rhythmic, soulful, liberating, and powerful. Connect breath, body, and soul with the miraculous, ecstatic, and powerful elements of nature and awaken to the wonder and awe of being alive and embodied! My hope is that our time together will remind you of the medicine that is gratitude, and leave you feeling empowered, wrapped in self-love, & vibrating at your highest frequency.

Artificial intelligence is not just changing jobs — it is changing what it means to have a job.

This session explores how AI agents, automation, and software platforms are transforming corporate work, professional careers, and entrepreneurship. Students will learn which skills are becoming obsolete, which are becoming valuable, and how roles are shifting from doing work to directing and supervising intelligent systems. The talk also introduces the emerging “one-person company,” new labor models, and how future workers may build businesses instead of applying for jobs. Attendees will leave with practical guidance on what to study, what to practice, and how to prepare for a career in the AI economy.

In short, what do do when:
\- Your Future Boss Might Be an Algorithm
\- Your Future Lawyer Might Be an Algorithm
\- Your Future Doctor Might Be an Algorithm
\- Your Future Teacher Might Be an Algorithm

title: MIAMI FAKE SHAADI BOLLYWOOD PARTY @LA OTRA
description: MIAMI FAKE SHAADI BOLLYWOOD PARTY @LA OTRA Miami's #1 desi party, @La Otra on Aug 21st, Fake Shaadi edition! Where Bollywood music meets Miami' nightlife! Absolutely no one. But we're throwing a wedding anyway- because why should baraatis not have fun? title: Flow & Stillness: A Yoga Journey
description: Join us for a nourishing afternoon that honors the complementary energies of yin and yang through movement, rest, and connection.
long_description:
Join us for a nourishing afternoon that honors the complementary energies of yin and yang through movement, rest, and connection.

About this Event

Flow & Stillness: A Yoga JourneyThis workshop invites you to explore the complementary energies of yin and yang through a thoughtfully curated yoga journey. We will begin with a dynamic vinyasa flow led by Ignacio Gajardo (@yogaignacio), awakening the body through breath-centered movement, strength, and mindful challenge. As the practice unfolds, we'll gradually shift into the quieter qualities of yin through longer-held postures and guided meditation led by Rachel Loren Abraham (@rachellorenabraham), creating space for reflection, nervous system regulation, and deep rest.
Following practice, we'll gather over refreshments to connect, reflect, and build community. 🙂

This workshop is designed to support:Greater balance between activity and restIncreased body awareness and presenceStress reduction and nervous system regulationMeaningful connection with communityA deeper appreciation for the interplay of effort and surrenderAll levels are welcome. Modifications and options will be offered throughout the practices.

Instructor bios:Ignacio Gajardo is a yoga instructor and meditation practitioner with over ten years of experience. Formed in India and Bali, his teaching blends organic movement, precise asana work, and an integral, breath‑centered approach. After teaching in several countries, he now shares his practice in Lyon, France, offering Vinyasa, Power Flow, Hatha, and Yin Yoga. His classes are known for being fluid, deep, and grounding, weaving together movement, pranayama, and mindful presence.
Rachel Loren Abraham is a coach, facilitator, and teacher dedicated to helping people live well. Based in Atlanta, she holds her RYT-200 with extensive training in Yin Yoga. long_description:
We welcome you to come experience our weekly Day of Mindfulness. Nestled next to nearly 1,000 acres of blooming wilderness, right in the heart of Charlotte, we will find ourselves together in the present moment. Come recharge, reconnect with yourself and others while basking in the Spring glow of the forest. We will sit, walk, breathe and share the beauty of the budding Reedy Creek Park. Also, although this meditation group (Sangha in Sanskrit) is based in the teachings of Vietnamese Zen Buddhist Master Thich Nhat Hanh of the Plum Village tradition, people of all faiths and those with no spiritual tradition are welcome.

We offer this event in the spirit of Dana (generosity of the heart), and there is no expectation for a donation. However, as we do have rent and bills to pay, everyone is welcome to donate money, food for the potluck or just help with washing up or cleaning up so that we can continue to offer this as a place of refuge for the whole community.

If you’d like to support the continuation of this space, you’re invited to register with a sliding scale contribution (*$15–$45*).

**Registration link:** [https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/donation-form/day-of-mindfulness-in-the-heart-of-reedy-creek-park](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/donation-form/day-of-mindfulness-in-the-heart-of-reedy-creek-park)

Our day will include:
**Guided and silent meditation**
**Mindful Somatic Movement**
**Songs that teach and remind us to practice mindfulness**
**Outdoor mindful walking in a beautiful forest setting (weather permitting)**
**A sharing, reading or video about the practice of Mindfulness**
**Group Dharma sharing**
**Potluck lunch**

If the weather does not permit outdoor activities, we may remain indoors.

Please arrive 5 to 15 minutes early so we can all arrive and settle in without too much commotion.

We will meet for more of a formal practice from 10am to 1:00pm.

title: We Rest as Reparations 2.0 – A Day of Rest with JC Jackson
description: We Rest as Reparations 2.0 – A Day of Rest with JC Jackson
long_description:
Six women rested at the first one. Chapter Two is open. Three hours of stillness, herbs, and the Sabbath we were never given.

About this Event

Chapter Two. Saturday, August 22, 2026. 2:00 to 5:00 PM. Jesse's House Holistic Assisted Living. Houston, TX.
On May 30, six women came to a house in Houston to rest. No agenda. No performance. Just lavender lemonade, a stretch, a sound bowl, an hour of protected sleep, and hot tea.
One of them left me this: "Phenomenal day of deep rest. Thanks sis."
That is the only review I needed to open the door again.
Chapter Two is for you if:
You are tired in a way that coffee does not touch. You give care to everyone and forget yourself in the doing. You have been told to rest but have not been shown how. You want a Sabbath your grandmothers were never given.
What we will do together:
Arrive to lavender lemonade and the Magnesium Sigh application on your wrists and the back of your neck. Stretch with Kiera for 30 minutes. Sit for spoken word and a sound bowl meditation. Take one full hour of protected rest, lights low, phones away. Wake up gently to hot tea, fruit, and a salve to take home. We close in a soft circle.
You will leave with a copy of the journal (if you choose the bundle) and Elijah's Ease salve made for the back of your neck.
Tickets:
Day of Rest only: $30Day of Rest + Journal: $50Journal only: $25 (Paperback)Salve Lab Add-On (1:00 to 2:00 PM, 15 spots): $30What to bring:
A comforter or wrap you love. A yoga mat or something soft to lie on. Comfortable clothes. A water bottle. An open heart.
Everything else is already waiting for you.
Limited to 30 guests. Once we are full, we are full.
This is not a workshop. It is not a lecture. It is the rest we are owed, taken on purpose, in God.
The door is open at werestasreparations.com.
JC

title: Splendor of Sitar with Purbayan Chatterjee
venue_name: Castro Valley Center for the Arts
description: Splendor of Sitar with Purbayan Chatterjee
long_description:
Purbayan Chatterjee is a highly esteemed and versatile sitar virtuoso, known for his exceptional skills and innovative approach to music. With a career spanning several decades, he has captivated audiences worldwide with his mesmerizing performances, effortlessly blending traditional Indian classical music with contemporary influences. Chatterjee’s profound understanding of his instrument and his ability to evoke emotions through his soulful melodies have firmly established him as a prominent figure in the world of Indian classical music.

Young and talented Amit Kavthekar has rhythm running through his veins. At the early age of six, he was being groomed in the art of playing tabla by the legendary Ustad Allarakha. He has also been fortunate enough to be taught tabla intricacies by Ustad Zakir Hussain--a maestro in Indian classical music an international phenomenon in the fields of percussion and world music.

**A 90-minute vinyasa flow journey in the fresh air of the Wasatch mountains**

Drop into meditation, move through a full vinyasa flow, and then drape a cool lavender towel over your eyes for an extended savasana.

**Saturday, August 22nd 9:30-11:00 am @ Brighton Ski Resort**

You’ll already be up the canyon, so bring a friend and a picnic for a hike! It’s a ready-made self-care day ❤️

**Reserve a spot with a donation (recommended: $15-25)**
Venmo @emcapito with the “Brighton August” and your email for updates, and you are absolutely welcome to just show up!

**This is a community offering, so if the budget is tight or it’s your first time and you’d prefer to decide if you’d like to donate after, everyone is invited!**

* Suitable for all levels.
* Bring your own mat, water and sunscreen/sunglasses.
* Dress in layers – Utah weather is unpredictable!
* I also recommend socks just in case your mat gets hot in the sunshine.
* Ages 12 and up. Minors must have a parent/guardian present.

**Plan travel time so that you have at least 10 minutes to settle in.** The canyon always takes a little longer than expected. Give yourself a cushion and enjoy the beautiful drive.

**DIRECTIONS:**
Map: https://goo.gl/maps/f3ffkpHRvF2GtVce7
Brighton is at the top of Big Cottonwood Canyon. We will meet on the patio on the back of the Milly Chalet, which is the first building on your right as you turn into the large Brighton parking lot. It’s one level and cream colored next to a lift.

**Questions? Lost?** Text 801-898-0842

**Many thanks to Brighton Resort** **for hosting us over the years!**

title: Suminagashi: An Art of Irreplaceable Moments
description: Originating in Japan more than 800 years ago, Suminagashi literally means “floating ink.” This elegant technique was first enjoyed in the Heian period (794–1185) as a courtly pastime, where artists and nobles would marvel at the delicate, ever-changing patterns created on water.In this class, you will learn how to gently drop ink onto the surface of water and guide the ripples with your breath, brushes, or even the subtlest movements of air. The resulting designs are then transferred onto washi
long_description:
Originating in Japan more than 800 years ago, Suminagashi literally means “floating ink.” This elegant technique was first enjoyed in the Heian period (794–1185) as a courtly pastime, where artists and nobles would marvel at the delicate, ever-changing patterns created on water.
In this class, you will learn how to gently drop ink onto the surface of water and guide the ripples with your breath, brushes, or even the subtlest movements of air. The resulting designs are then transferred onto washi paper and even onto fabric items such as handkerchiefs, creating one-of-a-kind works of art.
Because the process is simple, the class is fun for a variety of ages and skill levels. Each print captures a fleeting moment, never to be repeated, embodying the Japanese aesthetic of impermanence and beauty in transience. Children aged 8 and above are also welcome to participate.
Whether you are interested in traditional arts, meditation through creative practice, or simply wish to explore a new form of expression, this class offers a unique opportunity to connect with history while creating your own modern interpretations of this ancient craft.
About the Instructor
Ayakoh Furukawa (a.k.a Ayakoh Furukawa-Leonart) is a visual artist with a unique background who has mastered Japanese calligraphy and Western painting. She studied with Buddhist calligrapher Sougyu Kashimoto in Osaka, Japan, and is currently a member of the Metro New York Sumi-e Society. Besides the RESOBOX Sumi-e class, she has taught at educational and cultural institutions such as Lyceum Kennedy Japanese School and the Japan Society Summer program. She moved to New York in 2000 and studied Asian Art History at Hunter College, CUNY, where she received her Master of Fine Art in Studio Art. Her paintings and drawings have been exhibited internationally. Her deep knowledge of both Western and Asian arts offers an enjoyable experience of the Japanese art of Sumi-e.

long_description:
Join us at [The Foundry](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UkELFXvFLmenCGuY6), Black Room (Shop 5), for a brown bag lunch (you are welcome to bring a packed lunch and/or non-alcoholic beverage), as guest facilitator Yusuf leads our reading and discussion of one of Mir Taqi Mir’s iconic ghazals, [Ulti Ho Gain Sab Tadbiren](https://rekhta.org/ghazals/ultii-ho-gaiin-sab-tadbiiren-kuchh-na-davaa-ne-kaam-kiyaa-meer-taqi-meer-ghazals). You can use the dropdown menu on Rekhta to switch from the romanized version to Hindi or Urdu scripts. We will provide printed versions with embedded glossaries at the Meetup. If you have any issues accessing the poem, please DM Mariyam. You may also enjoy a rendition of the ghazal by [Begum Akhtar](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eEPcbMvKA0w).

***Facilitator Yusuf on Mir:***
*Thamthe thamthe thamaingay aansoo / Rona hai, kuch hansee nahin!*
(Tears will take time to stop / This is melancholy, not mirth).

*Khuda-e-Sukhan* (god of poetry) Mir Taqi Mir has always been my favorite Urdu poet. His poetry encompasses the deepest reflections on the human condition, his woes and ordeals authentic,
and his seeming disillusionment with society and humanity extremely palpable and heartfelt. I feel deeply that ‘our sweetest songs tell of saddest thought’, or in poet Maulana Hasrat Mohani's words *shīrīni-e-nasīm hai soz-o-gudāz-e-'mīr'* (Mir's tender sadness is like the sweet morning zephyr), and so Mir affects my heart and sensibilities like no other. I look forward to sharing his work with all of you!

***About the location:*** The Foundry is a community event space in Cambridge, and we will be in the Black Room (Shop 5).

* The Black Room is wheelchair accessible.
* There is parking on the surrounding streets: Rogers Street, Bent Street, Third Street, Fifth Street, among others. There are two accessible parking spots on Rogers Street in front of the main entrance.

long_description:
**GET READY FOR AN ARTISTIC VICTORY!**
Join the **World Chess Hall of Fame & Galleries, Saint Louis's** premier cultural destination, for a unique, approachable, **hands-on workshop**. This **family-friendly program** is a highlight of the local calendar and a fun way to experience **chess education** through **creative play**.

**The Program: Design a Sports Medallion**
Unleash your inner artist in our **Play & Create Space**. Attendees will **design and craft** their very own **custom sports medallion** to take home as a trophy of their creativity. Whether you are a fan of grandmaster strategy or athletic feats, this activity lets you express your personal style.

All supplies for this self-led activity are included, and **no chess experience is needed to join in!**

This program is complimentary for visitors and **World Chess Hall of Fame & Galleries Members! [Learn more about becoming a member.](https://worldchesshof.org/get-involved/become-a-member/)**

**The Exhibition: *Game Plan: The Strategy of Chess & Sports***
**The Intersection of Strategy and Culture**

This **fun** program is offered in connection with our current exhibition, ***[Game Plan: The Strategy of Chess & Sports](https://gemini.google.com/gem/e1737aec3cdb/0be28f2ce075eb04)***. This exhibition explores **the intersection of art and strategy in modern culture** by comparing the mental rigors of chess to the physical and tactical demands of sports. This event promotes **chess education** by demonstrating how the drive for excellence and the symbolism of victory—like a medallion—connect the worlds of the board and the field.

long_description:
In conjunction with Portland Paddle ,SMSKN is offering this workshop to members only interested in gaining experience paddling in dynamic waters and developing the skills to do so confidently. The group will seek out rough-water conditions in the exposed waters by Crescent Beach and develop skills related to rock gardening, surf landing/launching, reading rough-water environments, risk assessment, and rough-water rescue techniques.
**Trip Level: Intermediate**. This workshop is NOT designed for novice kayakers, should be comfortable with wet exits and T-rescues before participating.

**Bring your full kit:** Helmet (if you have one; let Suzanne know if you need one), kayak, paddle, apparel appropriate for occasional swims in 60-degree water, pfd, skirt, and secure footwear. If you have towing equipment that you'd like to practice with, please bring that too. And bring lunch!
Start time: Paddles wet by 09.30am at Crescent Beach We'll have some orientation time on the beach before launching.
**Register on MeetUp and then follow the link below to register and pay**
https://www.portlandpaddle.net/lessons/roughwater-ocean-paddlers/

**Skills Covered:**

* Surf launching and landing
* T-rescue practice in waves and inside rocks
* Self rescue practice in waves and inside rocks
* Towing

If you haven't already, please complete the SMSKN participant agreement online at [https://www.smskn.net/club-documents/1116-2/](https://www.smskn.net/club-documents/1116-2/)

long_description:
Join Nowhere Cinema for a coming of age double feature with a screening of Minding the Gap and Cleaners! Details for each are below!

Individual film tickets are pay what you can with a $6 minimum, or you can purchase a double feature ticket for a minimum of $10. Get your tickets here: https://www.nowherecinema.com/event-details/cleaners-2019

Cleaners (2019)
⏰ Break 8:45pm \| Start 9:00pm

"At a catholic high school in the Filipino city of Tuguegarao, a rambunctious batch of students rebel against all expectations to be good and clean."

I'll let Kani, the film distributors, explain why Cleaners is so special:
*"Every frame of filmmaker Glenn Barit’s Cleaners was printed, hand colored with highlighters, and then rescanned, giving each of its angst-drenched emotions a singular handmade texture and the whole film a bone-deep nostalgia for growing up in the Philippines in the early aughts. One-of-a-kind visuals, plus earnest tracks by Filipino emo band Typecast and a swelling score composed by Barit himself, compel us to feel the fullest extent of Cleaners’ all at once loud, soft, funny, and sweet teenage antics and affections." –* Kani

Minding the Gap (2018)
⏰ Doors 6:30pm \| Start 7:00pm

"Filmmaker Bing Liu searches for correlations between his skateboarder friends' turbulent upbringings and the complexities of modern masculinity."

Minding the Gap is one of the best documentaries I have *ever* seen. It's so deeply personal and honest. The way Bing Liu breaks down generational trauma and masculinity within his friend group is stunning.

title: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening
description: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening Classes will guide you through complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual wisdom. An ongoing in-depth course deliving into profound wisdom within Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Hindu/Indian/Vedic spiritual philosophy, and Upanishads. You can see prior recordings at: YesVedanta.com/bg2 Timeless Wisdom of Bhagavad Gita: A Complete Course in Non-Duality in 700 Verses Join us for an in-depth exploration of the Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Vedantic wisdom. Our weekly live Zoom classes will guide you through the complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual knowledge. The Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue between Krishna (the teacher) and Arjuna (the student), addresses life's deepest questions: What is the nature of the Self? What is the highest purpose of existence? title: Satyajit Ray's THE MUSIC ROOM (1958) + Live Raga Performance!
description: One of the cinema master's most revered films—a meditation on the all consuming power of music, with a a live Hindustani raga performance!
long_description:
One of the cinema master's most revered films—a meditation on the all consuming power of music, with a a live Hindustani raga performance!

About this Event

As part of 7th House's annual SEE•SOUND series celebrating the intersection of music and cinema, join us for an evening celebrating the mesmerizing artistry of Hindustani classical music, centered on THE MUSIC ROOM (JALSAGHAR, 1958), one of master filmmaker Satyajit Ray's towering achievements, accompanied by a live performance of "Miyan Ki Malhar," one of the ragas featured prominently in the film, performed by an ensemble featuring Thomas Klepper (sitar), Saheb Singh (tabla), and Anita Sinclair (tanpura).
Widely regarded as one of the great masterpieces of cinema, The Music Room is among the defining works of Satyajit Ray's extraordinary career. Released just a few years after his breakout film Pather Panchali (1955) introduced Ray to international audiences, The Music Room marked another major artistic leap for the legendary Bengali filmmaker. It follows Biswambhar Roy (Chhabi Biswas, one of Bengali cinema's most revered actors), an aging Bengali zamindar whose unwavering devotion to music endures even as his wealth, influence, and way of life steadily disappear. As the world changes around him, he retreats into the grandeur of his once-splendid music room, where lavish concerts become both an affirmation of beauty and a poignant refusal to let go of the past.
Adapted from Tarasankar Bandyopadhyay's celebrated short story, The Music Room was Ray's first film to extensively incorporate Indian classical music, weaving it directly into the emotional and dramatic fabric of the story rather than presenting it as an interlude. Featuring a magnificent score by legendary sitar maestro Ustad Vilayat Khan alongside breathtaking performances by some of India's foremost classical musicians of the era, the film transforms music into one of its central characters while exploring the tension between tradition and modernity

long_description:
This yoga class begins with the chuckle of Laughter Yoga exercises, which may seem unconventional, but are most uplifting. It provides the joy of laughing for participants who attend this exercise routine that combines laughter with deep yoga breathing.

The session is conducted by Pete & Jan Girard who discovered this mood-lifting technique and were highly motivated to follow it and teach others the magic of laughter. Their class is a mix of quick activities and participants take part in a variety of exercises, such as the laughter milkshake, the sprinkler and the woody woodpecker. All are meant to generate simulated laughter that targets breathing in the head, chest and diaphragm.

It goes beyond free-flowing humor as the whole experience is orchestrated to create a connection among the group members and to help them leave all inhibitions to get the full benefit. Most participants feel it is childlike, helps to let their guard down and keeps them in the present, which leads to feelings of genuine moments of joy.

Walk-ins welcome! You don't have to be an LHSC member or join this Meetup to attend. Don't be discouraged if there aren't many RSVPs; there are lots of folks who aren't on Meetup who will be there too!

long_description:
**Weekly Sunday Meditation Classes with Kelsang Delam**

Join us each Sunday for a guided meditation class designed to help you cultivate inner peace, clarity, and wisdom in the midst of everyday life.

Each class begins with a guided breathing meditation to calm the mind, release distractions, and create a foundation of inner stillness.

This is followed by the *Liberating Prayer*, a traditional Buddhist prayer that inspires compassion and positive intention.

Kelsang Delam then offers a practical teaching based on the current class series, sharing timeless Buddhist wisdom in a way that is accessible and relevant to the challenges and opportunities of modern life.

The teaching is followed by a second guided meditation, giving you the opportunity to deepen your understanding by reflecting on the teaching and bringing it into your own experience.

When time allows, the class concludes with a group discussion and an opportunity to ask questions, helping you gain greater insight and confidence in applying the teachings to your daily life.

After class stay for coffee/tea and community!

Whether you're new to meditation or have an established practice, these weekly classes offer a supportive and welcoming space to develop a peaceful mind and a compassionate heart.

title: Doggy Noses & Yoga Poses at Connecticut Valley Brewing Company
description: Join Us for Doggy Noses & Yoga Poses in South Windsor, CT to benefit Pack Leaders Rescue of CT.
long_description:
Celebrate our 9th anniversary with us by getting down(ward) dog on Day of the Dog!

About this Event

What is Day of the Dog:
August is traditionally known as the unofficial birthday for shelter animals whose day of birth may be unknown. August also happens to be DNYP’s anniversary month; so what better way to honor rescue pups than to host a country-wide event?! 
Join us for Day of the Dog at Connecticut Valley Brewing Company in South Windsor, CT to celebrate another year of raising funds and awareness for shelters and rescues through yoga and puppies! This class will combine the joy of yoga with the cuddles of adorable rescue puppies and dogs from Pack Leaders of CT. Pints and good times to follow your flow!
This class will be held outside, weather permitting.
Event Highlights:
45-Minute Yoga Class: A certified yoga instructor will lead a mixed-level yoga session while rescue puppies and dogs roam freely, providing cuddles and puppy kisses.15-Minutes of Snuggles: After yoga, enjoy a "snuggasana" session with the pups.Post-Yoga Pint: Relax in the tasting room with a pint or mimosa from Connecticut Valley Brewing Company. (for guests 21 and over).Tickets:
Advance Purchase: $49.50At the Door: $60 (space permitting)A portion of all ticket proceeds will be donated to Pack Leaders of CT.
Important Information:
Bring Your Own Mat: Please bring a yoga mat or towel.Limited Space: Space is limited, so order your Pawssport today!Respecting The Rescue: The only dogs allowed on the class floor will be the rescue and no food or treats will be allowed on the class floor.Spectators are NOT Allowed: To ensure the safety, privacy, and comfort of participants and event staff/volunteers.Event Participants: The recommended age is 12+ to attend the class, however, children who are able to behave appropriately in a yoga class are welcome with a legal guardian. We ask all event attendees to have a great time while remaining respectful of those around them.Join Us for a Fun and Furry Yog

This ritual is an invitation to pause, receive, and reconnect—offering a steady rhythm of care and recalibration as you move through the month.

🌿 Gentle arrival, grounding & intention setting

🧘‍♀️ Guided shamanic meditation for clarity and relaxation

A deeply calming blend of supported restorative yoga and soothing sound to help you Mat, blankets, bolsters and eye masks provided.

About this Event

If you need the kind of rest that feels like someone finally took the invisible backpack off your body, this one’s for you.
The Relaxation Ritual at Neutral Moon Studio is a blend of restorative yoga and sound bath for a deeply calming nervous system reset. You’ll be guided through supported postures designed to help the body soften, followed by soothing sound to help the mind quiet and the system downshift. This is your invitation to do less, receive more, and leave feeling held, rested, and a little more like yourself again.
Your Restorative Yoga Facilitator: Kelley Raye is a certified yoga instructor, nervous system regulation practitioner, and owner/founder of Neutral Moon Studio, an Atlanta-based wellness space designed for intentional movement, rest, and connection. She creates slow, grounding experiences that blend mindful movement, breathwork, somatic practices, and meditation to help women reconnect with their bodies and find more ease.
Your Sound Healer: Erica Ronelle is a certified sound facilitator and the founder of The Feeling Tone, where she offers sound experiences that support nervous system regulation, sensory relief, and embodied rest. Her sessions guide participants into a calmer pace, using intentional sound and gentle direction to help soften overstimulation and reconnect with the body. Drawing on a background in vocal training and instrumental study, Erica blends technique with sensitivity and care to create grounded, restorative experiences. Whether working with individuals or groups, she offers sound as a way to return to the body and listen more deeply.

What to Bring:
Yoga mats, bolsters, blocks and blankets are provided. Please bring a water bottle, and wear comfortable clothing you can move and breathe in. No prior yoga experience is needed.

long_description:
Join us for a journey of creativity, growth, and elevated spirit and well-being in this two-
part event.

Part 1: Self-Growth Improv: A Beginner Introduction led by Val Adlington is a
beginner-friendly improv class offering a playful and powerful pathway to personal and
spiritual growth. Through simple improvisation exercises, participants will explore how
being present, supportive, and flexible allows us to meet life as it unfolds—without
needing a plan or judging ourselves.
We will begin with a short-guided meditation to open the heart, helping us arrive
grounded, receptive, and connected—ready to both give and receive.
Improv gently teaches essential life skills: active listening, adaptability, emotional
awareness, and trust in yourself and others. By practicing the core improv principle of
“Yes, and…,” participants learn to accept what is happening and build forward with
curiosity rather than resistance. In a supportive, low-pressure environment, mistakes
are welcomed as opportunities, helping quiet the inner critic, reduce anxiety, and build
resilience.
This class encourages spontaneity, creativity, and self-confidence while strengthening
empathy and communication. Improv shows us that we don’t need to know the next
step to move forward—we just need to stay present. What emerges is greater self-trust,
deeper connection, and a renewed ability to navigate uncertainty with openness and
grace.

Part 2: A Laughter Yoga Experience is a brief introduction and then practice of
Laughter Yoga. For those not familiar, Laughter yoga (Hasya yoga) is an exercise
routine that combines intentional laughter with deep belly breathing, without any difficult
movements or relying on jokes or humor. Created in 1995 by Indian physician Dr.
Madan Kataria, it is based on the idea that your body cannot tell the difference between
fake and real laughter, providing the same physical and mental health benefits.

long_description:
**A Nature-Centered Sanctuary for Solo Visionaries**

Welcome to the Solopreneur Sanctuary, a monthly gathering designed specifically for independent business owners. This space is designed to foster genuine camaraderie, share knowledge of valuable resources and spark organic ripples of support that elevate the solo journey.

As a nature-centered business, we believe in gathering outside the traditional four walls whenever possible. Gathering in nature naturally lowers stress, encourages expansive thinking and provides a literal breath of fresh air. It's the perfect setting to step away from the digital world and connect with people who truly understand the solo business journey.

**What to Expect:**

* **The Resource Exchange:** Share knowledge of tools, tech, books, resources, contacts, insights, etc.
* **The Clearing:** A dedicated, supportive space to voice the unique daily heavy lifting of running a solo business, allowing you to let it go and reset in a safe, encouraging environment of peers.
* **Collaborative Ripples:** Explore light, organic ways we can create positive ripple effects and support each other without any pressure, expectations or financial exchange.

***Our Sanctuary Boundary:***
*To keep the space restorative and collaborative, we honor a strict "no unsolicited advice" policy. We are here to listen, celebrate, share resource knowledge and hold space for each other's journey, while allowing everyone to run their business their own way.*

We will be sitting under a canopy in the grass. If you prefer, feel free to bring something to sit on and make yourself comfortable. Don't forget a notebook and any tips, tools or contacts to share.

Meetup is informational. Register at:
**https://www.navigatetonature.com/event-details/solopreneur-sanctuary-2**

I'll see you in the wild!

title: The Meta Project: Designing for DT:DC
description:
**\* This is an in-person event**

DT:DC has spent years building a community of curious, skilled, civic-minded people. This workshop asks a new question: what could we accomplish together if we pointed that energy inward and built stronger connections between members outside of DT:DC events.

Using BJ Fogg's Behavior Design framework, developed at Stanford, we'll explore what a DT:DC professional network could look like, surface the best ideas from the room, and map out what it would realistica
long_description:
**\* This is an in-person event**

DT:DC has spent years building a community of curious, skilled, civic-minded people. This workshop asks a new question: what could we accomplish together if we pointed that energy inward and built stronger connections between members outside of DT:DC events.

Using BJ Fogg's Behavior Design framework, developed at Stanford, we'll explore what a DT:DC professional network could look like, surface the best ideas from the room, and map out what it would realistically take to make it happen.

Nothing is decided in advance. The aspiration is open: *what could DT:DC's professional network be and what positive impact could it have on DC and our DT:DC members?* Come with curiosity and leave with a plan.

This workshop is a bit meta: we'll use design methods to design for ourselves. Every person in the room is both participant and co-creator of the outcome.
**What you'll take away**
A hands-on understanding of the Fogg Behavior Model, one of the most practical frameworks for turning good intentions into real action. And something rarer: you'll have actually used it, on a real problem, with real stakes, in real time. As a community, we will walk out with a shortlist of project ideas we generated and prioritized together, plus a concrete behavior plan for moving the top one forward.

**Agenda**
**6:30 Networking**
**6:45 Welcome + framing**
What could DT:DC do and how tonight works
**7:10 Magic Wand brainstorm**
If DT:DC could do anything to create a professional network, what would it be? No filters yet
**7:25 Crispify the ideas**
Turn big dreams into specific, real-world behaviors and actions
**7:40 Focus Mapping**
Three rapid rounds: plot, cluster and prioritize what rises to the top
**8:10 Easify to make this actually happen**
Apply the Fogg Model to the leading idea: motivation, ability, prompt
**8:20 Debrief + next steps**
What did we decide? Who's in? What happens after tonight?

**WORKSHOP Facilitator**
**Ed O'Brien, Software Develope

looking for a place to become a better speaker, a more engaged listener, a more confident version of yourself… or whatever that looks like for you?

**Our weekly meetings are a supportive space where you can:**

* **Find your voice** and share your ideas with clarity, whether at work, at home, or in your community.

* **Get comfortable thinking on your feet** and answering questions without stress.

long_description:
Dear Illinois Prairie PUG members,

We received multiple positive reviews after our July meetup, so in August, we are going to have two talks again!
If you are wondering why we are having a meetup at the end of August, it's because [Djangocon.US](https://2026.djangocon.us/) is coming to Chicago! The event will take place on August 24-28 at Voco Downtown Chicago, and we wanted to use this opportunity to have a joint event.
If you know any Django developers who might be interested, please invite them!

We really liked Zach's presentation about pg_schema, and on August 26, we will hear from him again. He will present the talk **The Database flywheel.**
The second talk will be presented by Aayush Gauda:
**Can PostgreSQL Reduce Repeated Quantum Computation? Caching Quantum Simulation Workloads**.

*Agenda*

5:20 - doors open
5:30 - pizza arrives
6:00 - 6:10 - Hettie. Opening remarks
6:10- 6:40 - Zach. The Database flywheel.
6:45 - 7:15 Aayush. Can PostgreSQL Reduce Repeated Quantum Computation?
7:15 - 7:50 - Open discussion and networking
7:50 - 8:00 - Cleanup time and closing

**Speaker**: Zach Paden

Zach Paden is a tech lead at Symetra with experience ranging from scrappy startups and consulting to large regulated enterprises. His work spans data platform, analytics and application development where he’s seen more than his fair share of projects get bogged down or catch on fire due to their schema management practices.

**Talk Title:** **T***he Database flywheel*

**Talk description**

Devs often think a lot about how to have CICD when it comes to their application itself, but often rely on a shared dev DB to actually test code. We'll discuss how you can shift this left so that your database changes can be tested and validated BEFORE hitting any long-running instance.

**Speaker:** Aayush Gauba

Aayush Gauba is a researcher and open-source contributor whose work spans mathematics and physics. He serves as the Marketing Chair for DjangoCon US 2026 and organizes PyData

The Full Moon in Pisces illuminates the waters of our emotional world, inviting us to listen more deeply to our intuition, honor our sensitivity, and gently untangle the emotional ties that no longer serve our highest good. As with every full moon, this is a sacred time for release. Rather than forcing or striving, Pisces teaches us to let go with compassion, trust, and grace.

Sarah of Rays of Sunshine will begin the evening with insights into the astrology of the Full Moon before guiding you through gentle, nourishing movement and meditation, helping you settle into your body and prepare to receive. Throughout the ceremony, she will offer hands-on Reiki, supporting your nervous system, energetic release, and inner restoration.

As your body softens, Tommy of Soundularity will weave a celestial soundscape that mirrors the wisdom of water itself. Deep electronic textures invite you beneath the surface of the conscious mind, while heartfelt acoustic instruments carry you through waves of emotion toward spaciousness and peace. Like a flowing river, the sound becomes an invitation to wash away stagnancy, dissolve resistance, and rest in stillness.

Our ceremony unfolds outdoors beside a private lake in Lakewood, Colorado. Surrounded by water, you'll be held by the natural rhythms of the earth as the gentle presence of the lake reflects your own depth, fluidity, and capacity to return to calm.

long_description:
**A UC Irvine keynote on when human and AI teams outperform either alone**

RSVP using the link - https://luma.com/ww306wf3

Ascend GenAI, Orange County's professional community for generative AI, hosts an evening on the question every startup building with AI faces: which decisions should the model make, and which should stay with people?

Join them **Wednesday**, **August 26** from 6:00PM to 8:00PM at Merage Jewish Community Center of Orange County, 1 Federation Way, Irvine, CA 92603. Free on-site parking. Doors open at 6:00 PM; the program starts at 6:30 PM.

The keynote comes from Padhraic Smyth, Distinguished Professor and Hasso Plattner Chair in AI at UC Irvine. He is a Fellow of ACM, AAAI, IEEE, and AAAS, has published over 250 papers on machine learning and AI, and served as academic advisor to Netflix for the Netflix Prize. His research group studies human-AI collaboration: combining human and AI predictions so the pair outperforms either working alone, and learning which tasks to route to people and which to AI agents. His talk covers recent findings with direct application to teams deciding how much autonomy to give AI. A 15-minute open Q&A follows.

description: Join us for an evening of outdoor yoga as we explore what Yin yoga is — and what happens when we stop moving quite so quickly.
long_description:
Join us for an evening of outdoor yoga as we explore what Yin yoga is — and what happens when we stop moving quite so quickly.

About this Event

Yin yoga is a slower practice made up mostly of seated and lying-down poses that are held for longer periods and supported by the ground or with props to minimize muscular effort.
In this class, we’ll explore what makes Yin different from more active styles of yoga, what longer holds can offer, and why slowing down can be its own kind of practice.

long_description:
"A thrilling, transportative adventure that is everything promised—Chakraborty's storytelling is fantasy at its best." ― R.F. Kuang, #1 New York Times bestselling author of Babel and The Poppy War

"An exhilarating, propulsive adventure, stitched from the threads of real history, Amina’s adventures are the reason to read fantasy." ― Ava Reid, internationally bestselling author of Juniper & Thorn

Shannon Chakraborty, the bestselling author of The City of Brass, spins a new trilogy of magic and mayhem on the high seas in this compelling historical fantasy tale of pirates and sorcerers, forbidden artifacts and ancient mysteries, in one woman’s determined quest to seize a final chance at glory—and write her own legend.

Amina al-Sirafi should be content. After a storied and scandalous career as one of the Indian Ocean’s most notorious female pirates, she’s survived backstabbing rogues, vengeful merchant princes, several husbands, and one actual demon to retire peacefully with her family to a life of piety, motherhood, and absolutely nothing that hints of the supernatural.

But when she’s tracked down by the obscenely wealthy mother of a former crewman, she’s offered a job no bandit could refuse: retrieve her comrade’s kidnapped daughter for a kingly sum. The chance to have one last job and a final adventure with her crew, do right by an old friend, and win a fortune that will secure her family’s future forever? It seems like such an obvious choice that it must be God’s will.

long_description:
The Senior Market is growing fast and so are the opportunities! Join us for Senior Services Networking, a monthly group focusing on the opportunities of the Senior Market and on building partnerships and relationships for area Senior Market entrepreneurs and business owners!

Our Senior Services Networking Group meets monthly for lunch networking on the 4th Wednesday of each month from 11:45am-1pm. There are no requirements for attendance! Just show up and network with other contacts within the Senior Market.

Important Facts on the Senior Market...

There are over 100 million Baby Boomers and their parents. 76 million of them have or will soon reach retirement age, which means the senior population will more than double by 2030.

Adults aged 85 and above are the fastest-growing segment of the U.S. population.

Home health care is the fastest growing sector in the health care industry. Home health care spending will double from $50 billion per year to over $100 billion in the next ten years. One in every 20 people over 65 passes away each year. More than 2.5 million estates need to be settled every year. Over 43% of people will enter a nursing home during their lifetime. After a medical emergency or due to aging, more than 43% of people will face the decision of whether or not to enter into a nursing home or stay at home with some type of assistance.

Approximately 20% of seniors are using about 50 prescriptions every year! Over 61% of emergency room visits are by seniors, yet only 2% of these are nursing home patients. 81% of middle-aged couples over 55 years old own homes. Those in the top 10% of yearly income own homes that, on average, were built in the late 1970’s.

long_description:
Join the volunteers of NWA TechFest at GOAT LAB Brewery in Lowell, AR for free drinks and great conversations with other STEM professionals in Northwest Arkansas.

**Event Info**
August 26, 2026
6:00pm - 9:00pm

**Event Presentation**
6:30pm - 7:15pm

\-\-\-

**Meher Bhaskar Madiraju** will be presenting:

***"*From PoC to Production: Deploying Agentic AI at Enterprise Scale*"***

While many organizations are currently experimenting with LLM agents, bridging the gap between a local sandbox demo and a reliable, high-volume production environment is notoriously difficult.

My technical talk will bypass the high-level hype and walk the audience through the real-world engineering architecture required to make multi-agent systems robust. I will cover:
\- Architectural patterns for orchestrating multiple autonomous agents\.
\- Overcoming latency\, hallucination loops\, and compute bottlenecks in production\.
\- Applied MLOps strategies for safely testing and deploying agentic workflows\.

This will be a deeply technical, architecture-focused presentation. My goal is to share actionable, scalable engineering patterns with the NWA tech community so local engineers can successfully transition their own AI initiatives from PoC to production.

\-\-\-

*Do you have something you want to present at a later meetup? [If so, submit a presentation!](https://nwatechfest.org/speakers/)*

7:15pm - 7:30pm

\-\-\-\-\-

This recurring volunteer-organized event was created to give NWA STEM professionals the opportunity to meet, learn, and grow with one another to create a more connected community.

* Share ideas, opportunities, and resources

long_description:
\#\# Power and Perils of AI Aided Coding

* AI coding uses intuition, assistance, or rapid iteration to build software without traditional design formality. It can feel liberating and fast, but it comes with hidden risks. This session takes a closer look at both the advantages and pitfalls of this emerging approach.
* Attendees will explore when AI coding can boost creativity, collaboration, and speed, and when it can lead to fragile, hard-to-maintain systems. Through practical examples and guidelines, you will learn how to harness its strengths while avoiding the traps that undermine quality and long-term sustainability.

\#\# Format

* 6:30pm — Welcome & Networking: **Pizza, drinks and name tags will be provided—come hungry and ready to connect!**
* 7:00pm — Get people into the auditorium.
* 7:05pm — Orlando JUG and ODevs opening remarks.
* 7:10pm — *Featured presentation by guest speaker.*
* 8:20pm — Q&A + Social Time. **Two attendees will each win a JetBrains license (e.g. IntelliJ IDEA, CLion, PyCharm Pro, ReSharper, etc.) and 3 attendees will each win an O'Reilly book.**

\#\# Speaker

* **Dr. Venkat Subramaniam** is an award-winning author, founder of Agile Developer, Inc., an instructional professor at the University of Houston, and creator of dev2next conference.
* He has trained and mentored thousands of software developers in the US, Canada, Europe, and Asia, and is a regularly-invited speaker at several international conferences.
* Venkat helps his clients effectively apply and succeed with sustainable agile practices on their software projects.
* Venkat is a (co)author of multiple technical books, including the 2007 Jolt Productivity award winning book Practices of an Agile Developer. You can find a list of his books at <[https://www.agiledeveloper.com](https://www.agiledeveloper.com/)\>\.

Join us for an evening of deep rest, guided awareness, and sound.

This Full Moon gathering is an invitation to slow down, soften, and reconnect with yourself through the nourishing practice of Yoga Nidra. Yoga Nidra, often described as “yogic sleep,” is a guided practice that supports profound relaxation while inviting you into a space between rest and awareness. It is known for encouraging deep calm, self-awareness, and a state of conscious rest.

This experience also honors sound as a pathway into presence, inner listening, and deeper awareness. Woven throughout the practice, sound healing supports the journey inward by helping soften mental activity, settle the body, and create a more spacious experience of rest. Combined with Yoga Nidra, the sounds become a gentle companion, deepening relaxation and inviting a fuller sense of ease, rest, and being held in the practice.

This evening is for anyone who is seeking more rest, longing to reduce stress and anxiety, or wishing to deepen their connection with themselves in a supportive and restorative space.

*Mats and blankets are provided.

About this Event

Join us for this Friday night sunset edition of our signature class groove yoga & dance class.

We'll spend the first 45 minutes moving and breathing with the ocean, soulful beats, and our sweet community, and then transition to a 30 minute dance party at the ocean's edge 🌊✨

This all-levels creative vinyasa flow class moves through postures at a steady pace, cultivating a sense of connection within ourselves and our surroundings. The intention of this class is to create ease, joy, health and healing in heart, body and mind. With each class you will build strength, suppleness and flexibility.

Near the end of our practice we head down to the water’s edge for a dance party, inviting a playful and freeing aspect to your practice. You can expect an exquisitely curated soundtrack of music— from fun and familiar, booty-shakin beats, to soft, soulful tracks meant to soothe the heart, to other worldly sounds that are sure to inspire ecstatic expression— informing an ever-changing tapestry of movement and emotion.

With views of the Golden Gate Bridge, resting your eyes on the waves as you practice, and watching birds soar above, curated music and our incredible community - it’s truly a magical experience to be immersed in.

My classes are rhythmic, soulful, liberating, and powerful. Connect breath, body, and soul with the miraculous, ecstatic, and powerful elements of nature and awaken to the wonder and awe of being alive and embodied! My hope is that our time together will remind you of the medicine that is gratitude, and leave you feeling empowered, wrapped in self-love, & vibrating at your highest frequency.

long_description:
Arm Balance Workshop 

FRIDAY | AUGUST 28 | 6:30-8:30p

$35

Arm balances are liberating postures that teach us not only about our intrinsic power but about our innate playfulness, courage, fearlessness and agility. If you have fear or discomfort when attempting (or avoiding) arm balances, this workshop is for you.

During this exploratory arm balance workshop, we will systematically prepare the body for a variety of arm balances including crow, crane, one-legged crow, side crow, one-legged side crow, and fallen angel. You’ll learn how to thoroughly prepare the wrists, shoulders, core, and hips to find structural stability and strengthas well as utilize subtle energy of the poses as we learn how we can use breath, Drishti (gaze), and physics to bring balance and sustainability.

After warming the body through a flow, there will be time to experiment and play with these postures using props, one-on-one attention, and partner work before we finish class with an integrative Savasana.

Embrace play, power, and presence in this engaging workshop for people new to arm balances or are looking to layer on more variations into their practice.

Julia Britzius is an E-RYT with training in Mobility, Somatics, and Dance. She believes in the power of yoga as a pathway to deeper connection to self, which includes embracing physicality, experimentation, and PLAY!

long_description:
LevelUp is an event for people that are interested in technology, startups, entrepreneurship, community building, and networking in the Las Vegas Valley. LevelUp gives an opportunity to startup founders to present their companies to the community with immediate feedback, support, and mentorship from a panel of successful investors, entrepreneurs and other ecosystem leaders. The goal is to elevate each participant to the next level.

For 90 minutes the panel will hear presentations from local startups and then give feedback, ask questions, guide the founders to immediate next steps and even possibly invest in their business.
In addition to watching presentations, attendees will have the opportunity to mingle with other participants. It’s an evening to learn, connect, support, share, mentor, and inspire one another.

LevelUp is free and open to anyone interested in entrepreneurship regardless of their background or the stage of their company. We aim to facilitate a friendly and encouraging environment.

This event will be held periodically and will help grow the ecosystem by bringing the entrepreneur communities together to share entrepreneurial excitement, energy, and encouragement.

title: In-person class:Indian Cuisine: Butter Chicken and Naan (Los Angeles)
description: In-person class:Indian Cuisine: Butter Chicken and Naan (Los Angeles) Classic Indian Cuisine: Butter Chicken and Handmade Naan Discover the rich culinary traditions of Northern India in this hands-on cooking experience featuring two beloved classics: Butter Chicken and freshly made naan bread. Butter Chicken, known as Murgh Makhani, originated in Delhi in the mid-20th century when inventive chefs transformed leftover tandoori chicken into a luxurious tomato and butter-based curry. The result became one of India's most celebrated dishes, renowned for its velvety texture, delicate balance of spices, and comforting depth of flavor. In this class, you'll learn how to marinate and prepare tender chicken, build a rich and aromatic butter chicken sauce from scratch, and master the techniques for creating soft, pillowy naan bread with the perfect texture and char. Along the way, we'll explore the cultural significance and history behind these dishes while gaining confidence with traditional Indian spices and cooking methods. By the end of the class, you'll have the skills to recreate an elegant and authentic Indian meal at home—one that is both deeply rooted in tradition and perfect for sharing with family and friends. No experience is required! We provide all the equipment and ingredients, which are easy to find at local markets if you don't already have them in your home kitchen. Our events are casual and meant to be fun and instructive, not hardcore. This class is designed to be just as fun for the cooking enthusiast who wants to be a part of every step as it is for the first-timer who is happier observing and assisting (or taste testing). Any dietary restrictions Fish free Shellfish free

long_description:
**Join us on August 29 as we discuss** ***Ten Incarnations of Rebellion*** **by Vaishnavi Patel.**
**From the bestselling author of** ***Kaikeyi*** **comes a bold and imaginative novel that blends mythology, history, and fantasy into a sweeping story of resistance and revolution. Inspired by the ten avatars of Vishnu from Hindu mythology,** ***Ten Incarnations of Rebellion*** **reimagines these legendary figures across different eras, exploring what it means to challenge injustice, confront power, and fight for a better world.**
**Through interconnected stories that span centuries, Patel examines themes of duty, identity, sacrifice, and social change. Drawing on familiar mythological traditions while giving voice to characters often overlooked in the original tales, she creates a rich and thought-provoking narrative that feels both timeless and strikingly relevant to contemporary conversations about power and resistance.**
**Whether you're a longtime fan of mythology, enjoy speculative fiction, or are simply curious about modern retellings of classic stories, this book offers plenty to discuss. As always, we'll explore the themes, characters, and cultural context of the novel while enjoying great food and conversation.**
**Our discussions are welcoming and informal, and everyone is encouraged to participate at whatever level feels comfortable. Finished the book? Great. Only made it partway through? Come anyway. The conversation is always richer when we bring together different perspectives.**
**📖 Book:** ***Ten Incarnations of Rebellion*** **by Vaishnavi Patel**
**📅 Date: August 29**
**📍 Location: Peppino’s Dosa**
**Come for the fiction, stay for the food and fellowship.**

long_description: Join Molly for an afternoon of rest and sound healing. Restorative yoga is a healing practice of slowing down and moving into yoga postures with the support of props such as blankets, blocks, and bolsters. Restorative yoga activates the parasympathetic nervous system to promote deep rest and healing. The class will feel nurturing, relaxing, and regenerating. long_description:
This is unaffiliated but a free (donation-based) class that I’ve enjoyed so figured I’d post the info for anyone interested in joining in! The space is very attuned for meditation and spiritual practice. Again, I’m just a fellow student!

From their website:

Experience the Unique Power of Himalayan Yoga

As taught by the yogis from the Himalayas— Himalayan Yoga combines gentle postures, breathwork, and mindful relaxation techniques to connect body, mind, and spirit resulting in healing from within. Whether you’re new or experienced, this practice will leave you feeling relaxed, focused, and rejuvenated.

Benefits of Himalayan Yoga:

🌿 Enhanced flexibility, balance, and holistic strength
🌿 Tools/Techniques to cope with stress, anxiety and bring mental clarity
🌿 Energizing breathwork to uplift and restore overall health

💲 Pricing: Heartfelt donations ($10 suggested or pay what your heart desires and what you can…). All donations will go to support The Meditation Center.

📍 Location, parking & other essentials: The Meditation Center (TMC), 631 University Avenue NE, Minneapolis, MN 55413. Free parking is available across the street from TMC in the Church’s parking lot. Bring a water bottle. Yoga mat, pillows and blankets provided. Please arrive 5 minutes early and get comfortable in “the Hall of Tradition” on the main floor. No registration needed.

About Your Instructor:

Sunita Bhardwaj Gangopadhyay brings 18 years of affiliation in the Himalayan Yoga and meditation tradition. She has completed a 200-hour Teacher Training Program with Himalayan Yoga. Dedicated to helping students find balance and peace, Sunita focuses on making each class accessible and rewarding, regardless of experience level. Sunita has a PhD in Physics and a retired executive who worked in high tech industry for 25 years. She is currently the president of the Board at The Meditation Center. Native of India, Sunita currently lives in Eden Prairie, MN. She is married with two children.
